## 2026-09-05 -- PLA-450 + PLA-451: SIX DUPLICATE-ID MERGES, TWO HELD ON TAXON, THE CELERY BLIGHT SPLIT, AND THE FIRST PREDICTED MOVE OF `actionable` (CONTENT release; `95e66f6d` -> `36d6df6b`) [Claude Code]

**ONE promote, NINE `id` leaves, nothing else moves.** `tools/promote_pla450_451_problem_ids.py` (spec at `tools/staging/pla450_451_problem_ids/spec.json`), suite **63/63**, harness **42 injected / 42 caught / 0 survived / 0 broken** (anchor preflight 42/42, positive control green, sentinel reddened). Six crops touched: artichoke (3 leaves), asparagus, basil, strawberry, swiss-chard, celery (2). Full write-up: `docs/2026-09-05-pla450-451-problem-id-merge-outcome.md`. **Commit HELD for Trevor's approval.**

**ORDER WAS T1 FIRST.** UC IPM's celery early-blight page names *Cercospora apii* and says "do not confuse this disease with the early blight disease that occurs on tomato and potato, which is caused by an *Alternaria* species"; its late-blight page names *Septoria apiicola* and says it "is not the same as late blight of tomato and potato caused by *Phytophthora infestans*, which does not infect celery". PLA-451's attribution, which came from claude.ai knowledge, CONFIRMED on the crop's own cited anchors. `celery-early-blight` and `celery-late-blight` minted; display names untouched (they are the celery-literature names); both pairs registered in `problem_id_registry.json` with the organism-level reason.

**SIX OF PLA-450'S EIGHT MERGED, TWO HELD.** The taxon check (the rule that a join-key reuse needs an organism check, not a name check) refutes two of the eight. cilantro's `bacterial-leaf-spot` names *Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *coriandricola* in its own `cause_seasoned` and on its cited WSU Mt Vernon anchor (read today; WSU adds two less-common *Xanthomonas* pathovars specific to coriander); the peppers' `bacterial-spot` is *Xanthomonas*. edamame's `bacterial-blight` names *P. savastanoi* pv. *glycinea* (its ISU anchor; UMN read today, which also lists snap and lima bean as hosts of that pathovar); the beans' `bacterial-blights` names *X. campestris* pv. *phaseoli* and *P. syringae* pv. *phaseolicola* (Clemson, read today, no soybean). Different pathogens on both pairs: merging would CREATE the defect PLA-451 fixes. The promote carries both as `HELD` and REFUSES a spec row on either (refusal spec, mutation-proved). Both stay OPEN and UNREGISTERED in the collision gate on purpose: a decision Trevor has not made stays visible. Decision-ready options in the outcome note; recommendation is the scoped mint the celery pattern uses (`cilantro-bacterial-leaf-spot`, `edamame-bacterial-blight`). The six merged: cutworm -> cutworms (asparagus), flea-beetle -> flea-beetles (swiss-chard), japanese-beetle -> japanese-beetles (basil), botrytis-gray-mold -> gray-mold, twospotted-spider-mite -> two-spotted-spider-mite, snails-and-slugs -> slugs-and-snails (artichoke), slugs -> slugs-and-snails (strawberry). Majority-wins is a GUARD: each `to` must sit on more crops than its `from`, counted from the pre-state.

**THE PREDICTION WAS PINNED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN AND MATCHED.** PLA-450's addendum asks for the post-promote collision figures to be predicted, not read off. From the 42-pair list and the gate's own normalization: eight OPEN pairs retire because their minority id ceases to exist (five two-id merges plus the three-pair slug family), no registered pair names a retired id, and each celery mint adds one NAME_SHARED pair against the generic id it left ('blight early' == 'blight early'), both registered. **Predicted 42 / 20 / 22 -> 36 / 22 / 14; observed 36 / 22 / 14.** `check_collision_prediction` runs the REAL gate on the post state and refuses any other figure, and the suite pins the same literals independently so a retuned constant reddens. A pair-by-pair test asserts the exact eight that vanish and the exact two that arrive.

**THE VARIETY JOIN WAS MEASURED WITH THE RIGHT SHAPE.** `varieties` is a dict with `recommended[]`; a list-shaped walk returned 0 and would have read as "no consumers". The real count is **129** (apple 102 on apple-scab / cedar-apple-rust / fire-blight / powdery-mildew; strawberry 22 on anthracnose / red-stele / verticillium-wilt; asparagus 5 on asparagus-rust / fusarium-crown-rot / purple-spot). **None sits on any id this promote touches**, so asparagus's `cutworm` and strawberry's `slugs` carried no reference and the direction question PLA-450 raised is moot. Both states pass the resolve check; the retired-id arm is a refusal spec.

**A57 STAYED GREEN THROUGH THE REWRITES.** `verify_post` checks ladder presence BEFORE the generic field loop (the first draft had it after, where the field-equality check masked it and the driver failed for the wrong reason -- the earlier-check-masks-guard pattern, fixed at authoring). Every rewritten entry keeps its ladder byte-for-byte. **Gauntlet:** `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all six with A57 green; `gate_all` **121/121**; `control_ladder_gate` 0 integrity / 0 unladdered; `variety_resistance_gate` 0; `variety_ladder_delta_gate` 0; `register_completeness_gate` PASS; `release_verify` clean, exactly the six declared crops changed, lettuce-leaf byte-identical, no top-level or catalog delta. **Collision suite RE-MEASURED to 36d6df6b** (`tools/test_problem_id_collision_gate.py` 27/27; its harness 28/28 caught): the six merged decisions are asserted by the ABSENCE of the minority id (never by the absence of the pair), the two held pairs by presence + open + unregistered, and check 3 (FAMILY_MEMBER), which lost its only live exercise when the slug family merged, is driven on a scratch copy that restores the family with two id writes.

**ARTICHOKE, REVIEWED AS ONE CROP.** Its 11 problem entries (and asparagus's 5) are the only FOUR-KEY entries in the roster: `id`, `type`, `name`, `control_ladder`, no cause/symptoms/prevention, no severity, no sources (every other entry carries 8 to 16 keys). That is WHY the binomials sit in `name` ("Gray mold (Botrytis cinerea)"): there is no `cause_*` field to hold the organism. The three variant ids are merged; the remaining eight were reviewed against the roster (artichoke-plume-moth, artichoke-aphid, artichoke-curly-dwarf, black-tip, bacterial-crown-rot are correctly crop-scoped or singletons; cutworms, powdery-mildew, verticillium-wilt already sit on the majority id). Naming is PLA-453 and out of scope; the schema gap is reported, not fixed.

**THE JULY-CERT DUPLICATE SCAN (report only).** The 2026-07-02 cert waves touched the problem arrays of 30 crops. Per wave, the only entries added whose normalized name already existed on the crop are the three pear duplicates batch 26 retired (pear scab on both pears, Fabraea on pear-european, all in `73a1f64`). Live canonical carries 0 within-crop name duplicates across all 128 crops. A looser same-token / same-binomial scan over the 30 crops produced 30 candidate pairs, all read, all distinct problems (squash bug vs squash vine borer, peachtree vs lesser peachtree borer, and so on). **The pattern did not recur.**

**PLAYBOOK.** `docs/ladder_batch_playbook.md` 5a: the collision-gate re-measure is a REQUIRED close step, with the "add registered, never open" assertion and the predict-before-run rule for promotes that are supposed to move `actionable`.

**Not verified / out of scope, by name:** PLA-457, PLA-448 s4d unbundles, monitor_and_tolerate, PLA-453 naming (artichoke's parentheticals included); the two held pairs await a ruling; `bacterial-soft-rot` spans *Pectobacterium* on cilantro and "*Pectobacterium* / *Pseudomonas* species" on cauliflower, an umbrella by both entries' own wording, noted not filed. ## 2026-09-05 -- PLA-8: THE COVERAGE FLOOR ARMS AS A57, AND THREE INSTRUMENTS BREAK UNDER IT (canonical UNCHANGED at `95e66f6d`)

**TOOLING ONLY. No crop record touched, `LATEST.txt` not bumped, no promote, nothing for `release_verify` to verify.** Full write-up: `docs/2026-09-05-pla8-coverage-floor-armed.md`.

**THE LAST DEFERRAL OF THE ARC IS CLOSED.** `control_ladder_gate.coverage_violations` is wired into `whole_crop_gate` as **A57**, failing as `control-ladder-coverage:`. A56's own header said the floor "arms when the rollout actually lands, which is `control_ladder_gate`'s own stated INV-1 condition," and the playbook said arming it on 2026-08-22 would have taken `gate_all` from 121/121 to 7/121. Batch 27 landed the condition at 913 of 913. **PLA-8 IS DONE.**

**THE UNIT IS THE PROBLEM ENTRY, NOT THE CROP, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE DESIGN.** "Every certified crop carries a ladder" would sit red at 121 of 128 forever, because the seven shells carry `pests: []` / `diseases: []` and hold **zero entries to ladder**. Entry-scoped, they pass with NO carve-out at any certification status -- and that also **answers the question `ea3f91b` left open**, in the guard's tests where that correction said the answer belonged: a crop that certifies carrying zero problems is LEGAL, because there is nothing unladdered about it. `[]` stays A56's "laddered and left blank" defect; A57 owns ABSENCE only, so one defect is never named twice. Measured on `95e66f6d` BEFORE arming, so the arm is not a bet: 913 entries, **0 with the key missing, 0 `None`, 0 `[]`**. A57 arms green by construction.

**THE MICROGREEN SCHEMA WAS BUILT AGAINST, NOT ASSUMED.** Eight crops carry `name_beginner`/`name_seasoned` and no `name` (PLA-452), and instruments have gone blind there twice on the record -- PLA-449's collision gate reported both minted ids BLIND when narrowed to `("name",)`, and `ladder_batch`'s own load-bearing-field test SURVIVED dropping the microgreens half of `PROSE_FIELDS`. So: the floor prints `problem entries scanned: 2` on wheatgrass (a scanned count on every crop, so a zero is never an unmeasured zero); it labels off `problem_id_collision_gate.DISPLAY_NAME_FIELDS`, **imported and not retyped**, so an entry with neither `id` nor `name` reports as `wheatgrass/Tray fuzz` and never `?`; and both properties are mutation-tested **on wheatgrass specifically**.

**PROOF IT CAN FAIL: `tools/mutate_a57_coverage_floor.py`, 8 injected / 8 caught / 0 survived**, graded through the FULL `whole_crop_gate` rather than the standalone module. Families: key deleted, set to null, both again on the microgreen schema, a new unladdered entry appended, the same with no `id` at all, a SHELL gaining an unladdered entry, and **a whole new certified crop appended to the roster** -- the shape that beat four PLA-162 guards at once. **Three instruments, because "fail a commit" is a claim about all three:** `whole_crop_gate` fires A57; `gate_all` FAILS naming `ghost-crop`, a crop absent from the base roster; `precommit_release_verify --base/--candidate` reports **BLOCKED**. Liveness: positive control green, sentinel reddens or the run exits HARNESS DEAD, and a MUTATION-APPLIED marker read off the STAGED tree **at the crop the defect lands on** -- grading the roster addition on its donor would have reported a clean apple and called the guard blind. The shell refusal spec carries its own positive control, because "the seven shells pass" is otherwise equally consistent with the floor never having looked at them.

**DEFECT 1: `tools/mutate_a56_reachability.py` HAD BEEN EXITING `HARNESS DEAD` ON EVERY RUN SINCE 2026-08-24, AND NOBODY RE-RAN IT TO SEE.** That is the liveness defense working exactly as designed and then waiting. Its sentinel stripped every ladder to `[]` and asserted A56 stays SILENT -- correct on 2026-08-22, when empty was indistinguishable from absent, and false from 2026-08-24 when `ladder_violations` gained the `[]`-is-a-defect check, so the harness read its own correct catch as a mis-armed coverage floor. Repaired rather than deleted: `[]` must now REDDEN A56 (the sentinel the PLA-215 convention asks for) and a `None` ladder must redden A57 and NOT A56 (the separation). **This is the same class as batch 25's dead harness reporting 34/34, and the fix for that class is re-running the harness, not writing it.**

**DEFECT 2: WITH THE HARNESS ALIVE, ITS COHERENCE MUTATION REPORTED AS A SURVIVOR -- AND THE MUTATION WAS WRONG, NOT THE GATE, FOR THE SECOND TIME.** It put `balance_nitrogen` on apple-scab, which was `insect_soft_bodied` only when picked on 2026-08-22 and which the catalog has since widened to `['insect_soft_bodied', 'fungal_foliar', 'fungal_soilborne']`, making the injection LEGAL. The first version of this same mutation used `raise_soil_ph` and went stale the same way. **A hard-coded method name is a record of what the catalog looked like once, and the catalog is the gate's own input**, so it now DERIVES its victim at run time (any cultural method disjoint from `TYPE_TARGETS['fungal']`, HARNESS DEAD if none exists) and prints what it picked (`avoid_ammoniacal_nitrogen ['physiological']` today). Tightened in the same pass: **each mutation now asserts its OWN guard's message**, not merely that A56 went red, because grading on "the gate fired" lets a mutation be scored as caught by a different family than the one it aims at. **After repair: 10 injected / 10 caught / 0 survived.**

**DEFECT 3, AND IT WAS MINE: PUTTING THE FLOOR IN `all_violations` REDDENED 29 PINNED PROMOTE SUITES, AND ONLY THE 45-MINUTE FULL-TREE RUN FOUND IT.** The first cut added `coverage_violations` to `control_ladder_gate.all_violations`, on the sound-sounding reasoning that a guard whose entry point is never called is a zero with extra steps. `gate_all` stayed 121/121, both harnesses passed, the standalone gate reported 0, the targeted tests were green -- **every check that ran against TODAY'S data agreed it was fine.** The full tree went from the documented 5 failures to **33**, twenty-nine of them one assertion repeated: `GateContract::test_control_ladder_gate_clean_on_post`, `assertEqual(CLG.all_violations(_post()), [])`, failing with *"First list contains 190 additional elements"*. Those suites replay a HISTORICAL post-state, and batch 20's carries 190 unladdered entries **because that is what a rollout in progress looks like** (88 of 121 laddered at that moment). Widening the function made 29 suites assert something FALSE about their own moment. **The rule this broke is the one A57 itself was careful about -- do not arm a gate on data it reddens -- applied to a surface I did not think of as data. A pinned fixture is data.** Fix: `all_violations` stays INTEGRITY-ONLY, its established meaning; the floor is reached from the two places that police the SHIPPING roster, A57 (per crop, enforced roster-wide by `gate_all`) and `main()`, which now prints a separate `COVERAGE FLOOR:` section and counts it toward the exit status (`0 integrity violation(s), 0 unladdered problem entries`). The trap is written into the docstring and pinned by a test, because the next reader to notice the floor missing from the aggregate will otherwise "finish the job" and redden all 29 again.

**THE ARC'S OWN TOOLING, REPAIRED RATHER THAN SKIPPED.** Batch 27's handoff filed `test_ladder_batch.py` (1 failure + 6 errors) as "the arc is complete" and left it as a decision. Both were `todo` emptying. The failure -- `test_there_are_unladdered_crops_left_to_measure` -- is retired and inverted on the instruction the class's own docstring left behind when its PREDECESSOR's denominator emptied on batch 5, and now asserts the arc-complete fact **cross-walked against A57**, because `lb.laddered` is the weaker predicate (ANY problem carrying the key marks the crop done, so 3-of-5 reads as laddered while carrying 2 coverage violations) and that gap is exactly what the floor closes. `test_no_true_twin_group_remains_on_the_roster` is now **dormant, not dead**: it re-arms itself the moment an unladdered certified crop exists again. Measured for the record and NOT acted on -- repointed at all 121 certified crops instead of `todo`, `family_cut` finds THREE twin groups (field-corn/flint-corn/popcorn, yellow-summer-squash/zucchini-courgette, dry-bean/green-beans-bush), the sibling sets the arc deliberately propagated across, so repointing would arm the test RED on correct data. The six ERRORS are fixed by building an unladdered SCRATCH target rather than skipping the class: skipping was the wrong repair, because those tests protect a defect that has recurred twice (`best_use[:150]` in `cmd_prepare`, `[:104]` in `cmd_verify`) on methods this arc actually confused, and a skipped suite protects nothing. Note the ladder keys must be DELETED, not nulled -- `lb.laddered` tests key presence.

**GAUNTLET.** `gate_all` **121/121**; `whole_crop_gate` PASS; `control_ladder_gate` **0 integrity / 0 unladdered, 913 of 913**; `register_completeness_gate` PASS; A57 harness **8/8**; A56 harness **10/10**; every PLA-8 promote suite re-run **3,218 passed**; `test_ladder_batch` **27 passed**; canonical byte-identical to `LATEST.txt`. **Full tree: 4 failed, 5,148 passed, 1 skipped (43 min)** -- from 5 failed / 6 errors / 5,141 passed at the batch-27 close. The remaining four are pre-existing and none are this work's: `test_bare_host_scan`'s stale pinned population, `test_cited_claim_scan`'s 8-of-28 uncached allium URLs, and `test_problem_id_collision_gate`'s two, still keyed to `PINNED_SHA = ce98b0a6` while canonical is `95e66f6d`, two promotes on. **That last one is NOT re-pinned here on purpose**: the handoff's ruling stands, it should move onto `promote_fixture.pre_state` rather than keep pinning live canonical, and it is PLA-449's task.

**UNCOMMITTED.** Seven files changed plus two new (`tools/mutate_a57_coverage_floor.py`, `docs/2026-09-05-pla8-coverage-floor-armed.md`), awaiting Trevor's approval per CLAUDE.md.

## 2026-09-04 -- PLA-8 BATCH 27, THE MICROGREENS: the arc closes, and the gate it armed (`ba61762a` -> `95e66f6d`)

PLA-8 BATCH 27 -- arugula-microgreens, broccoli-microgreens, cilantro-microgreens, pea-shoots, radish-microgreens, sunflower-sprouts, wheatgrass (`ba61762a` -> `95e66f6d`; ONE promote, SEVEN crops). Roster laddered **114 -> 121**. **PLA-8 IS COMPLETE.** 43 rungs, 85 register strings, 14 problems, catalog UNCHANGED at 64, zero prose edited: the promote is purely additive, putting `id` + `type` + `control_ladder` onto 14 entries for 42 changed leaves.

**THE COMPLETION TEST IS EVERY PROBLEM ENTRY, NOT EVERY CROP, and the arithmetic is stated because an instrument cannot state it.** 913 of 913 problem entries on the 121 certified crops now carry a ladder, up from 899 of 913. **121 laddered + 7 shells = 128.** The seven shells -- avocado, olive, oyster-mushroom, shiitake-mushroom, lions-mane-mushroom, wine-cap-mushroom, button-mushroom -- carry `pests: []` and `diseases: []` with `verification_status.status = None`. Present and empty by intent, per CLAUDE.md. They hold ZERO problem entries, so any instrument counting laddered-vs-unladdered by problem id passes straight over them and will never report them as owed. That is why the count is written down here rather than left to a tool.

**ZERO IDS MINTED, WHICH WAS THE BATCH'S CENTRAL CLAIM AND IS THEREFORE A GUARD.** `fungus-gnats` and `damping-off` are both REUSED: `microgreens-mix` is laddered on this same schema and carries both, and `damping-off` is carried by 14 crops. `check_ids_are_reused` refuses any pinned id that does not already live outside the batch AND on the precedent crop. The PLA-449 collision guard ran at id-pinning time, BEFORE fan-out, against POST-APPLY data: **42 pairs -> 42 pairs, zero introduced, zero removed.**

**THAT ZERO IS A REAL ZERO BECAUSE THE INSTRUMENT WAS PROVED LIVE FIRST, on a difference and not a clean report.** A probe stamped `damping-off-microgreens` and `fungus-gnats-microgreens` onto the seven and ran the guard both ways: WITH the PLA-449 schema fallback (`DISPLAY_NAME_FIELDS = ("name", "name_seasoned", "name_beginner")`) it produced 2 OPEN findings, `damping-off` <-> `damping-off-microgreens` on FAMILY_MEMBER/NAME_SHARED and `fungus-gnats` <-> `fungus-gnats-microgreens` on NAME_SHARED; with the fallback narrowed to `("name",)` it produced **0 findings and reported both ids BLIND**. `damping-off-microgreens` is edit distance 11 from `damping-off`, so check 1 never reaches it either. The fallback is exactly what closes the hole, and it was confirmed BEFORE pinning, not after.

**THE BUNDLING RULE WAS APPLIED AND ANSWERED AGAINST DOCUMENTS, NOT WAIVED FOR CONVENIENCE.** Four of the seven disease names bundle mold with damping-off ("Damping-off (and surface mold)", "Damping-off and surface mold", "Damping-off and mold in the seed mat", "Mold and damping-off"), and PLA-448 4d plus batch 26's pomegranate precedent (an id-less bundle SPLITS rather than minting a new bundle) both pointed at a split. It does not split, because the documents refuse the distinction. Penn State's microgreens page: "Damping-off is the only disease or pest issue we have encountered", with a figure captioned "Damping-off possibly caused by Rhizoctonia or Botrytis species in a microgreens tray". Virginia Tech SPES-756 names damping-off plus mildews and never uses the word "mold" at all. No readable .edu/.gov document attributes seed-mat fuzz to Rhizopus, Mucor, Aspergillus or Penicillium; the word "saprophytic" appears in none of them. Minting a `surface-mold` id would have asserted an organism-level distinction that the two most authoritative sources contradict -- the shape of the field pulling a fabricated entry out of the batch. So: ONE complex, ONE id. The bundled NAMES are PLA-453 and were carried byte-for-byte. Grey literature (Purdue, Missouri State) does list mold as its own management line item, which is what a future naming/scope ruling has to weigh; it is recorded, not acted on.

**THE SEVEN CROPS' PRE-BATCH GREEN WAS VACUOUS, AND THAT IS MEASURED.** `control_ladder_gate.identity_violations` and its type/applies_to checks all `continue` on any problem whose `control_ladder` is `None`, which every one of these 14 entries was. So `whole_crop_gate` reported PASS on all seven while checking nothing about their problems. Proof, not inference: the SAME sabotage (`type: 'not-a-real-type'` on wheatgrass's disease entry) returns **GATE: PASS on the pre-promote state and GATE: 1 VIOLATION on the post-promote state**. Landing the ladders ARMED the gate on seven crops it could not previously see. A shape gate cannot notice absence unless absence is spelled out, and here absence was the whole population.

**NO MATERIAL RUNGS, ENFORCED AS A SAFETY REFUSAL SPEC.** All 43 rungs are cultural or physical. `check_no_material_rungs` refuses anything above `physical` on these crops, because they are cut at cotyledon stage inside 7 to 28 days and eaten whole and raw (wheatgrass is juiced raw), and a pre-harvest interval on a 10-day crop is a different safety problem that this batch is not the place to solve. Nothing in any source or any crop's prose pushed toward a material rung; all seven authors reported the prose asserting the opposite ("there is no rescue spray for a raw cut crop"). The guard is quiet on the real batch, and its quiet is a PASS only because the mutation suite reddens it on an injected soft_chemical rung.

**THE MUTATION HARNESS EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN.** Suite **53/53**; harness **36 injected / 36 caught / 0 survived / 0 broken**, anchor preflight 36/36 matching exactly once, positive control green, sentinel reddened. The first run had **one survivor**: `copy/similarity_made_asymmetric`, because `test_similarity_is_symmetric` used a synthetic string pair that was symmetric anyway, so deleting the both-orders `max()` changed nothing. A vacuous test that read as coverage. It is repinned on a real pair (arugula's and broccoli's fungus-gnat `management_seasoned`) which difflib scores **0.288 one way and 0.828 the other**, a gap of 0.540 -- and the test now asserts that a one-order guard MISSES it (0.288 is under the 0.70 threshold) while the correct guard catches it, so the mutation is detectable by construction.

**WHAT THE COPY AND HOUSE-STYLE GUARDS CAUGHT IN AUTHORING.** 15 of 85 authored notes were rewritten after the verbatim-lift guard fired: THREE were lifted from the PRECEDENT's own rung notes (microgreens-mix is a shape exemplar, not a donor), and one was a **0.776 recombination against TWO different precedent rungs with no shared six-word run at all** -- the multi-donor pattern a run-length check alone cannot see, which is why the guard runs a both-orders ratio alongside the n-gram check. A narrow exemption was added for runs containing a NUMBER, because "7 to 10 day grow-out" has no honest paraphrase and demanding one would have been a guard refusing correct input. Then FIVE more notes were rewritten after the house-style guard caught internal machinery vocabulary in consumer prose: "so the ladder stops at the cultural rungs by design", "this rung earns more on cilantro", "this rung is doing more work". A reader of the app has no concept of a rung.

**TWO AUTHORING DIVERGENCES ADJUDICATED, ONE KEPT AND ONE CUT, BOTH ON EVIDENCE.** (1) Six authors declined the precedent's third gnat rung, `yellow_sticky_traps`; cilantro kept it. KEPT, and verified rather than accepted: cilantro's `management_seasoned` is the ONLY prose in the family that asserts traps ("sticky cards help you catch a building population early"). A scan of all eight microgreens crops found the other apparent hits were "sticky-when-wet seed" and "traps moisture". Note the precedent `microgreens-mix` carries a sticky-trap rung its OWN prose never asserts, filed below. (2) The wheatgrass author accepted "do not over-soak the seed" into `sound_sowing_practice` while the pea-shoots author refused materially the same advice ("drain the soaked seed well before sowing") as unplaceable. CUT, for consistency: two authors reaching opposite conclusions on one question is exactly where a batch invents a difference with no source behind it. Wheatgrass went 5 rungs -> 4, and "no catalog method covers pre-sow seed handling" is filed once, covering both crops.

**FINDINGS FILED, NOT FIXED** (this is a ladder batch; the prose is not its to edit). The root-hair-versus-mold diagnostic on radish-microgreens, sunflower-sprouts and wheatgrass is unsourced against `psu_microgreens`, these entries' only cited source, which is silent on root hairs; it sits in BOTH management registers, so a correction touching one sentence would leave the claim live, and radish's beginner "usually harmless" is the same claim class again. All seven fungus-gnat entries cite only `uc_ipm` PN 7448, a general pest note, while asserting crop-specific tray practice and cycle-length claims. `microgreens-mix` carries a `yellow_sticky_traps` rung with no prose backing. `unr_ext`'s catalogued URL 302-redirects to `naes.unr.edu/dfi/`. Four catalog gaps, each reported independently by multiple authors, which per the playbook makes them the catalog's problem and not the authors': no tray/equipment sanitation method (all seven leaned `garden_sanitation` past its end-of-season-debris definition), no pre-sow seed handling method, no method meaning "rinse the mat" or hull removal, and no cultural airflow method legal on insects (so every crop's "keep air moving" survives only as prose inside a `bottom_watering` note).

## 2026-09-04 -- ROSEMARY CERT-LOG CORRECTION: the PNW page was finally read, and "Phytophthora-only" is retracted (`132980d5` -> `ce98b0a6`)

ROSEMARY CERT-LOG CORRECTION -- batch 25's last owed data item (`132980d5` -> `ce98b0a6`; ONE promote, ONE appended string, ONE crop). The 2026-07-06 cert log recorded rosemary's root and crown rot as "correctly Phytophthora-only (UC IPM, Pythium already dropped)". **The PNW Plant Disease Handbook's rosemary root-rot page, which 403s to every direct fetch path this project has, was finally retrieved during batch 25** and names *Pythium*, *Berkeleyomyces* sp. (formerly *Thielaviopsis basicola*) and *Rhizoctonia* and **no Phytophthora**, so Pythium was dropped on a reading the document does not carry. **APPENDED, NEVER EDITED**: `verification_log_ref` is an append-only cert-dated historical record, so the original 900 characters survive byte-for-byte as an exact PREFIX (the promote refuses otherwise) and the correction is appended in the convention's `[CORRECTION <date>: ...]` form, 900 -> 1787 chars. **THE CAVEAT IS PART OF THE CORRECTION**: that page was reached through a text proxy plus a corroborating search snippet, which is two consistent retrievals and NOT a first-party read. Enough to retract an over-claim, a move toward saying LESS; NOT enough to assert those three genera, and nothing in the dataset does. Rosemary's rot stays pinned to the problem-class umbrella `crown-and-root-rot` and its consumer prose names no genus, which this correction confirms was the right call rather than merely the cautious one. Suite 16/16; **mutation harness 9 injected / 9 caught / 0 survived / 0 broken** after one survivor exposed an unreachable serializer (the write format was inlined in `main()`, which no test called, so a switch to `indent=2` survived the whole suite; `serialize()` extracted and driven). Gauntlet: `whole_crop_gate rosemary` PASS, `gate_all` **121/121 PASS**, `doc_roster_claim_gate` 0.

**WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE PROMOTE AND NOT PART OF BATCH 25.** The batch touched seven crops' problem entries; this touches one crop's cert log, a field with its own append-only convention and its own failure mode. Folding it in would have put a historical-record edit under guards written for ladder content, and `verify_post` would have had to accept a prose leaf moving on a crop whose entries were also moving, which is exactly the ambiguity the declared-correction scheme exists to remove.

**THE FINDING'S PROVENANCE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE FINDING.** The PNW page had been recorded as NOT READ twice in this session's own verification log, after 403s on every URL form, both sandboxed and with the sandbox override, and with a live archive snapshot that would not fetch. A reviewer reached it through a text proxy and corroborated it against an independent search-index extended snippet, then said plainly that it had never touched the origin. That honesty is what bounds the correction: it retracts an over-claim and licenses no new one. The opposite handling, treating a proxy read as a first-party read, is how a cached verdict becomes a false presence, which this repo has already paid for once.

**IT ALSO VINDICATES A CALL MADE WITHOUT THE EVIDENCE.** Batch 25 pinned rosemary's rot to the problem-class umbrella because the taxon was contested, and the rosemary authoring agent went one step further and stripped Phytophthora from `cause_seasoned` on the reasoning that the prose should not assert in words what the id declines to assert. The document agrees with it. The catalog's "water molds AND FUNGI" phrasing turns out to be load-bearing too: two of the three organisms named are true fungi, not water molds.

**HARNESS LESSON, the same one twice in one day.** The single first-run survivor was a mutation switching the canonical write to `indent=2`. It survived because the write format was inlined in `main()`, every driver read the file from disk, and nothing called `main()`. Extracting `serialize()` made it reachable and the mutation reddened immediately. Batch 25's suite had the identical shape in its base-SHA driver, which asserted the constant without calling the function that checks it.

## 2026-09-04 -- PLA-8 BATCH 25, THE HERBS: the first batch to RESHAPE the arrays; roster 101 -> 108 (`a9c84847` -> `500a6126` -> `132980d5`)

PLA-8 BATCH 25, THE HERBS, LANDED (`a9c84847` -> `500a6126` catalog -> `132980d52dd2f4c7850729401fdcfde8b5485ab0eb03f734e9acf949755d27b4`; TWO promotes; lavender, lemongrass, mint, oregano, rosemary, sage, thyme). **THE FIRST PLA-8 BATCH THAT RESHAPES THE ARRAYS RATHER THAN ONLY ADDING TO THEM**: 3 entries RENAMED, 4 bundles SPLIT into 9 limbs, 1 bundle half DELETED, 2 entries RETIRED, on Trevor's rulings of 2026-09-04. **36 canonical problems -> 38**; roster laddered **101 -> 108**; rungs 3338 -> 3479; entries carrying an id 823 -> 861; control_methods steady at 64; source_catalog 219 -> 220. Record corrections rode IN the batch rather than in a preceding round, because on these crops the correction and the authoring are the same work: **248 declared field corrections, each carrying its own reason and its own anchoring sentence**, and a `verify_post` that refuses any prose leaf that moved without a declaration (293 leaves changed, every one pinned or declared). **61% of this batch's records were unsourced at the start (22 of 36 entries, with rosemary, sage and thyme at 100%), and 22 of 22 came back SOURCED -- zero unsourceable.** PLA-448 §4f is ANSWERED AND HAS TWO ANSWERS: oregano's bare "Rust" is one organism nobody pinned (Puccinia menthae, renamed "Mint rust", T1-anchored at psu_ext + rhs), while lavender's bare "Leaf spot" is a genuine umbrella (US extension names one organism in a bulk list with no symptoms or management), so a mechanical pin-every-bare-generic rule would have been wrong half the time. `mint-rust`/`oregano-rust` are correctly TWO ids on host-specialized races, registered with the cross-inoculation evidence graded JOURNAL-ONLY rather than leaned on. **The PLA-449 collision guard was wired in at id-pinning time before fan-out**, its pass condition a DIFFERENCE rather than a clean report: 34 pairs on canonical -> 37 post-apply, **3 introduced and all 3 adjudicated and registered, 0 unregistered**; the 34 inherited are PLA-448 §4a's duplicates the batch only joins. Suite 61/61; **mutation harness 34 injected / 34 caught / 0 survived / 0 broken**, reached only after the harness caught FOUR vacuous tests of its own (a symmetry pair that was not asymmetric, an autojunk driver a verbatim copy is invisible to, a base-SHA test that asserted a constant without calling the function, and stale bytecode letting the suite import the CLEAN module). Gauntlet: `gate_all` **121/121 PASS**, all seven crops PASS, `control_ladder_gate` 0, A54 0, `register_completeness` PASS, `release_verify` clean with exactly the seven declared crops changed (its one remaining concern is the known section-E false novel key: `plantings_provenance` is byte-identical to base and lives on 1540 region cells across 118 crops). **FILED FOR TREVOR, NOT FIXED**: `control_methods.horticultural_oil` tells the reader to keep sulfur and oil 2 weeks apart while its own anchor UC IPM PN 7405 says **30 days**; `sulfur` says 2 weeks and IS faithful, to PN 7406, because UC IPM's two Pest Notes disagree. 76 rungs / 42 crops carry that method and 15 shipped notes state the figure in prose. See `docs/2026-09-04-pla8-batch25-herbs-handoff.md`.

**DETAIL THAT DOES NOT BELONG ON THE LEAN SURFACE.**

**Why the record corrections rode IN the batch.** Batch 24 corrected records in four separate promotes and then authored from them, which was right there. Here it would have meant authoring the same sentences twice: splitting mint's powdery-mildew/anthracnose bundle requires writing new prose for both limbs whatever else happens, and 22 of 36 entries had no anchor at all. The price of combining them is `check_corrections_anchored` plus a `verify_post` that matches every changed leaf to a pin or a DECLARED correction carrying its own `why` and `anchor`. 293 leaves changed; every one accounted for.

**Retirement is DECLARED, never inferred from absence.** `pinned_ids.json._retired` names both entries with reasons, and `check_reconcile` requires every canonical problem to be carried, renamed, split-from, or declared retired. Absence is exactly what a one-directional walk cannot see (the PLA-162 shape), so a retirement that is merely missing from the target would otherwise pass silently.

**The two retirements, and the evidence class that justified each.** lemongrass's "Generally pest-resistant (aromatic-oil deterrence)" was an assertion of ABSENCE wearing a pest entry's shape, and a walk of all 128 crops / 912 problem entries found it was the ONLY entry of its kind in the dataset. thyme's "Foliar fungal problems in humid weather" rested on an INFORMED absence rather than a failed hunt: CSU GardenNotes #731 names diseases for eleven herbs under one editorial hand and gives *Thymus vulgaris* one line, "Do not overwater due to root rot susceptibility". A reviewer later found two more admitted sources landing the same way, including a PNW handbook with NO thyme host entry at all.

**The five-crop root-rot decision.** Shared display names hid different organisms. Rule applied: reuse the existing problem-class umbrella whose display name matches, UNLESS the crop's taxon is resolved AND narrower. sage and oregano -> `root-and-stem-rots`; rosemary and thyme -> `crown-and-root-rot` (parsley's own record defines that id as exactly this umbrella, "Pythium, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia"); lavender alone mints, because its taxon IS resolved and narrower (*P. nicotianae*, dedicated WSU source) and its display name already names the genus.

**The PNW page that blocked rosemary was finally read**, by a reviewer, through a text proxy corroborated by an independent search snippet: "Pythium, Berkeleyomyces sp. ... and Rhizoctonia are among the organisms found." **No Phytophthora.** That makes the genus-agnostic pin CORRECT rather than merely cautious, and the rosemary authoring agent's decision to strip the genus from prose was right for a reason nobody could confirm at the time. STANDING CAVEAT recorded in the handoff: a proxy retrieval plus a snippet is two consistent retrievals, not a first-party read. Strong enough to keep an id decision and to say LESS; not strong enough to name those genera in consumer copy, and nothing does. The 2026-07-06 cert-log line calling rosemary's rot "Phytophthora-only" is OWED a `[CORRECTION]` append.

**THREE TOOLING DEFECTS OF THE ORCHESTRATOR'S THAT THE FAN-OUT CAUGHT.** (1) The suite's tier table was retyped rather than imported and had `biological` and `soft_chemical` inverted, which would have mis-ordered every ladder. (2) The per-crop validator read pinned `type`/`severity` to check ladder legality and never compared the OUTPUT's own values, so a file reverting oregano's spider mites from `mite` to `insect` -- the exact defect the batch exists to fix -- validated GREEN; measured by mutation, by the agent. (3) The validator's coverage walk compared output names to CANONICAL names, which cannot work for a batch that splits and renames, and produced 5 spurious refusals on mint alone. A fourth was in PROSE: the authoring brief told all seven agents `prune_out_infection` cannot reach fungal problems, which is false at the gate -- and when the orchestrator corrected it, mint and rosemary independently DECLINED the method anyway on its own catalog text ("a spotted leaf picked off ... that is garden sanitation and not this"). Gate-legal is not method-correct.

**TWO GUARDS WERE REFUSING CORRECT INPUT, and neither is findable by mutation** because the branch fires exactly as written. `check_no_shipped_prose_echo` flagged "go easy on the fertilizer.", which appears on **13 shipped rungs**; 75 short strings are already duplicated inside canonical, so the fix was a measured house-phrasing exemption (2+ donors; 760 of 10491 distinct sentences, 7.2%) that still catches all 9731 single-donor sentences. `LADDER_VOCAB` refused "The same care applies to a division handed over the fence" by matching `applies[_ ]to` with an optional space.

**A NEW GUARD, `check_no_multi_donor_recombination`**, closes a defect the ratio cannot see: a note assembled from two donors resembles NEITHER closely enough to cross 0.70. This batch's real instance scored under threshold against both. Measured before building rather than guessed: "shares a rare 6-gram" flagged 108, mostly ordinary English collocation. Its first brake (set nesting) was WRONG and an authoring agent caught it by READING the runs -- one stock sentence with a single word changed between copies ("at this step" vs "at this point") shifts the window set so neither nests, and a house phrase read as two donors. Replaced with POSITIONAL OVERLAP and verified both ways.

**`gate_all` went 0 of 121 on ONE catalog entry.** A54 requires a document-scoped id to carry a `title` read off the document itself; the `uc_ipm_pn7493` admission carried only a `name`. Every certified crop failed on it, which is what a roster-wide source-catalog check looks like when it fires. That entry accumulated THREE defects before it was right, each caught by a different mechanism: a reviewer found its `citable_for` asserting an unchecked absence (7406 carries the dormant-season sanitation sentence verbatim, so the admission's strongest-sounding argument was false), an authoring agent found it scoped away from the very crop class the orchestrator then told it to cite, and A54 found the missing title. Both promotes were reverted and redone rather than patched.

**FILED, NOT FIXED, and it is a safety figure.** `control_methods.horticultural_oil` says keep sulfur and oil 2 weeks apart; its own anchor UC IPM PN 7405 says **30 days**. `control_methods.sulfur` says 2 weeks and IS faithful, to PN 7406. **UC IPM's two Pest Notes disagree**, so oregano deliberately ships two different intervals on one crop, each faithful to its own anchor, with a loud note that a harmonizing sweep would introduce an error. ## 2026-09-02 -- ROW-COVER SAFETY: the trap precondition carried into the beginner register on 7 shipped crops (`c24d7754` -> `f851dc15`)

ROW-COVER SAFETY: **THE TRAP PRECONDITION CARRIED INTO THE REGISTER A BEGINNER READS** (`c24d7754` -> `f851dc15`; ONE promote; **10 registers across 7 crops**; catalogs steady at 64/219; problem and rung totals **byte-identical at 913/3244**, since the promote can only APPEND). **COVERING GROUND THAT GREW A SUSCEPTIBLE CROP LAST YEAR DOES NOT MERELY FAIL: IT SEALS THE EMERGING FLIES IN WITH THE CROP.** UMN's root-maggot page, fetched and READ, says it outright -- "Do not place row covers if onions or other root vegetables were planted in the same area the previous year" -- and it covers both *Delia antiqua* and *D. radicum*. Eleven shipped rungs recommend row cover against a soil-pupating maggot. FOUR carried the precondition in both registers; of the rest **SEVEN omitted it from `note_beginner`** and **TWO (broccoli, bok-choy) from both**. The advice most likely to be followed uncritically was the one missing the warning, on high-traffic crops: broccoli, cabbage, kale, brussels sprouts, collards, kohlrabi, bok choy. **NOT A NEW SOURCED CLAIM, hence NO source changes** -- every affected crop's own prevention prose already says "avoid spots where you grew cabbage-family plants last year", and four siblings already ship this sentence; the promote closes an internal inconsistency. **THE PROMOTE CAN ONLY APPEND**: each replacement must carry its original as a literal prefix, so it is structurally incapable of rewriting shipped prose. **THE COVERAGE GUARD ASSERTS ALL ELEVEN RUNGS AFTERWARD**, including the four it does not touch, because fixing seven and declaring victory is how the next pass finds the same defect again. Suite 58; **harness 43 injected / ZERO survivors** across 8 families. **THE HARNESS FOUND THREE DEFECTS IN THE GUARDS THEMSELVES, none a broken branch**: the similarity ceiling could be loosened 0.70 -> 0.99 undetected because the duplicate driver injected IDENTICAL clauses (1.000), which any ceiling short of 1 refuses (replaced with a paraphrase at 0.859, constant now pinned); removing `autojunk=False` changed nothing because the real clauses are 141-162 chars and autojunk engages at 200 (added a 226/244-char driver scoring 0.494 on, 0.834 off); and the touched-crop check was **VACUOUS**, accumulating evidence by iterating the pin table and comparing it to a set derived from that table -- deriving it from the diff was not enough, it stayed dead behind the per-edit check that fires first, and only reordering it AHEAD makes it catch the right NUMBER of registers changed on the WRONG crops. The suite separately caught two matcher bugs no mutation would have: `brassica\b` does not match "brassicas" (it refused a correct clause) and the enclosure pattern allowed no object between the verb and "in", so "seal emerging flies in" -- shipped house phrasing -- did not match. ## 2026-09-01 -- PLA-8 THIN-LADDER BACKFILL: 8 rungs onto 6 shipped problems; the scan's four false positives are the finding (`4f33522c` -> `b118f19d`)

PLA-8 -- **THIN-LADDER BACKFILL: 8 RUNGS ONTO 6 SHIPPED PROBLEMS, AND THE FIRST PROMOTE IN THE ARC THAT EDITS ALREADY-LADDERED CROPS** (`4f33522c` -> `b118f19d`; ONE promote; beet, fig, garlic, strawberry; catalog steady at 64, `source_catalog` byte-identical, no other crop touched). **EVERY ONE WAS FOUND BY THE THIN-LADDER SCAN, AND THE SCAN'S REAL VALUE WAS ITS FALSE POSITIVES.** Population: 775 laddered problems / 3,149 rungs, of which 133 carry two rungs or fewer. A thin ladder is NOT itself a defect, so the check was narrower: the prose names a control that EXISTS in the catalog, is LEGAL for that problem's type, and is missing from the ladder. Instruction phrases generated leads and **every hit was READ**: 10 leads over 9 problems, **6 real and 4 false**. **All four false positives failed for one reason: the prose names the control in order to DISCOUNT it** ("Research into tolerant varieties is ongoing but there is no home cure" on both huanglongbing records; "Few home varieties carry useful resistance" on cantaloupe bacterial wilt; and chamomile's "well-drained" sitting inside a descriptive aside about where gray mold does not occur). **A keyword scan cannot tell "do X" from "X will not help here" and 40% of its hits were the latter, so this must NOT be automated into a gate.** The reassuring half: 10 leads across 133 thin ladders means the thin population is overwhelmingly thin for good reason. **THE SIX FIXED**: `strawberry`/`red-stele` gains `improve_drainage` and `certified_clean_stock` (its prose leads with "Plant in well-drained soil or raised beds, buy certified plants"); both fig problems gain `prompt_harvest`, whose own `best_use` literally names "fig souring" as its case; `beet`/`common-scab` gains `even_watering` and `lower_soil_ph`, the first of which only became LEGAL in r9 and the second only EXISTED from r8; `garlic`/`botrytis-neck-rot` and `garlic`/`fusarium-basal-rot` each gain `cure_and_store`, minted in r8. **Two of the six were unfixable a day ago**, which is the argument for having run the catalog rounds first. **THE GUARD SHAPE IS INVERTED, BECAUSE "ALREADY LADDERED" HAS BEEN A REFUSAL IN EVERY BATCH SO FAR AND IS THE PRECONDITION HERE**: `expect_before` pins each ladder's exact current sequence so a drifted ladder REFUSES rather than being silently rebuilt; every pre-existing rung must be BYTE-IDENTICAL after, dict for dict; the record prose must not move at all; and the rungs added must be exactly the declared set. **`expect_before` earned its place immediately** by refusing the first dry run: I had taken fig's ladder order from the scan's SORTED output rather than the real sequence, and the guard caught it before anything was written. **EVERY ADDED RUNG MUST BE WARRANTED BY ITS OWN RECORD.** `check_warrants` requires a declared phrase from the problem's own prose for each new rung and asserts it is actually present, which is the restate-the-record discipline made checkable: a rung whose warrant is not in the record is an invention, however plausible. **It is the guard that would have caught all four false positives**, none of which could have produced a phrase that survived reading. **THE HARNESS RETURNED SIX SURVIVORS AND EVERY ONE WAS A DEFECT IN MY TESTING, NOT IN THE PROMOTE**: three drivers were hedged across branches that share one constant (`expected 7` appears in both `check`'s message and `check_warrants`'), two guards were only reachable by calling `verify_post` and `apply_to` DIRECTLY rather than through `check`, and **the `main` wiring driver passed with `check()` cut out of `main` because it used a sabotage `verify_post` ALSO catches**. That last one is the r8 lesson recurring one round later in a subtler form: it is not enough to reach the guard through the entry point, the sabotage must be one that ONLY that guard can see. Re-run: **49/49 both runners, harness 41 injected / ZERO survivors** across 6 families, preflight 42 anchors, positive control GREEN, sentinel RED. One FORWARD assertion (the post-state rung count, fixed by construction once every ladder is pinned to its `expect_after`) is documented in the promote and WITHDRAWN from the harness rather than left reported as a permanent gap. Batch 19's `check_cross_batch_divergence` was written one batch earlier and would have REFUSED this correct batch, because it assumed a shared id carries one ladder shape unless pinned. Six instances this batch, verified against the data, on top of batch 17's plum defect and batch 18's lemon index-page defect. The shape is consistent: **a crop's problems share ONE source id whose URL is specific to ONE of them.** That is mechanically detectable -- flag any node whose cited URL names a pest or disease absent from that problem's own name and prose. Worth building; deliberately NOT scoped into a crop batch, because a repoint is its own change with its own blast radius.

five co-occur with `beneficial_predators` and the exclusion precedes in all five. **THE MECHANISM IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT AS A STRING**: the sources say exclude ants SO THAT natural enemies can work, physical < biological delivers that ordering by construction, so the guard asserts the TIER as well as the order and refuses if `ant_exclusion` is ever re-tiered off `physical`. **THE SHARED-ID DIVERGENCE RULE, SETTLED HERE: a shared id MAY carry different ladders where the RECORDS differ; it may NOT carry different SHAPES for the same asserted content.** 10 shared ids, 9 match method-for-method, `citrus-aphids` diverges by exactly one rung and that is PROSE-GROUNDED, not two agents guessing: lemon's own sooty mold entry says "Managing ants, which protect those insects, is part of the same fix" and names aphids among them, while lime has no sooty mold entry so that sentence exists nowhere in its record. `citrus-canker` was the other shape and was COLLAPSED: `prune_out_infection` means taking the cut back into clean tissue and implies a curative excision the entry explicitly denies ("There is no cure for an infected tree"), so `garden_sanitation` won -- the rung would have contradicted the sentence it restates. **FOUR ID REFUSALS, EACH VERIFIED AGAINST THE RECORDS**: generic `aphids` (50 vegetable crops) refused because both citrus entries describe a CTV-vectoring complex; `spider-mites` (twospotted-focused, 15 crops) refused because lemon names citrus red mite AND twospotted with DIFFERENT monitoring seasons and the generic would lose the red mite half outright; `anthracnose` (14 crops) refused and lime proves why on its own record, carrying *C. gloeosporioides* and *C. acutatum* as SEPARATE problems; `bacterial-spot` refused for citrus canker, which is *X. citri*, not the peppers' Xanthomonas leaf spot. ONE reuse, `mealybugs` from chamomile, recorded honestly: chamomile's `cause_seasoned` is EMPTY, so the join rests on both entries being generically named rather than on a taxon match. **CITRUS `type` IS MIXED, UNLIKE STONE FRUIT, AND THAT CHANGES THE GUARD**: 21 of 24 problems ALREADY carry a fine type and must be PRESERVED EXACTLY, only 3 are coarse upgrades and those are pinned by name, so a fourth cannot ride along. Batch 17 could assert a clean coarse -> fine upgrade because all six of its crops were coarse; asserting that here would be FALSE. The preservation half is the one that matters -- a silent retype moves which methods are legal on the problem and no other guard would notice. **NO RUNG STATES A TEMPERATURE**: the crops' scale entries say oil is unsafe above 95°F, the catalog's `horticultural_oil` caution says 90°F, and the mite entries carry no figure at all yet their rungs had imported one. Ruled FOR THE RUNGS ONLY -- the method's caution carries the figure, so the stricter number governs by construction and no rung contradicts its own method. This does NOT resolve the conflict, which still renders from the crops' own `organic_treatment_*` prose on the same page; filed as a sourcing question. Suite **79/79 under BOTH runners**; **HARNESS 50 INJECTED, 51/51 ANCHORS EXACT, POSITIVE CONTROL GREEN, SENTINEL RED, ZERO SURVIVORS**, families schema/types/ids/sooty/ants/divergence/temps/vocab/materials/validate/blast/catalog/mechanics. **A NEW GUARD FAMILY THE PREVIOUS SUITES COULD NOT REACH**: the two refusals protecting `control_methods` and `source_catalog` live in `main()`, not in `check()`, and batch 17 tested them by comparing serializations FROM THE SUITE -- which asserts the OUTCOME without ever driving the promote's own guard. `CatalogUntouchedInMain` reaches them by sabotaging `apply_to` after a clean apply and running `main()` on a temp fixture; both branches caught. Gauntlet: `gate_all` **121/121**, `control_ladder_gate` 0, `register_completeness` PASS, `whole_crop_gate` PASS x2, `release_verify` **clean** against a same-class reference. **THE 16 SECTION-E CONCERNS AGAINST THE DEFAULT ANNUAL REFERENCE WERE VERIFIED, NOT WAVED OFF**: both crops' `regions` subtrees are BYTE-IDENTICAL base -> candidate, all four "novel" keys already sat in 16 base cells, `lettuce-leaf` lacks three of them entirely, and the only top-level keys this promote changed on either crop are `pests` and `diseases`. NEXT: sweet citrus (grapefruit, mandarin-clementine, orange-navel; 32 problems), not yet prepared. **THE LARGEST REMAINING CATALOG GAP IS NUTRIENT SUPPLEMENTATION**, which has no method at all -- lemon's `iron-zinc-deficiency` ladder is a single `even_watering` rung while chelated iron and zinc, citrus micronutrient fertilizer, EDDHA on high-pH soil and foliar spray are all unplaceable. Bigger than ant exclusion was: it affects every physiological disorder on the roster.

### Carried forward, NOT closed by this batch

Five adjudications were made during the read and remain open as sourcing/content work:

1. **Oil temperature, 95°F vs 90°F.** Ruled for the RUNGS only (no rung states a figure, so the method's caution carries it and the stricter number governs). The crops' 95°F still renders from their own `organic_treatment_*` fields, beside the 90°F caution, on the same page. Needs a real sourcing pass against the citrus documents.
2. **lemon's phytophthora entry contradicts itself on the mulch setback**: `prevention_seasoned` says "a foot", `prevention_beginner` says "a hand's width". Roughly 3x apart inside one record.
3. **lime anthracnose's BEGINNER register carries a flat absolute** ("Persian limes are not affected") where its SEASONED register hedges ("appears to be immune"). The authored rungs keep the hedge in both registers, so the ladder and the existing beginner prose now disagree. The existing prose is the thing that should change.
4. **Phytophthora is typed `fungal` while its own prose says "water molds, not true fungi".** No oomycete type exists and `fungal` is the only bucket reaching `improve_drainage` and `resistant_rootstock`, so it is correct-by-necessity, but the record contradicts its own field.
5. **A mis-pointed-key defect**: lemon's mealybug and sooty-mold entries make ant claims citing only `ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/GARDEN/FRUIT/citrus.html`, which was READ and is an INDEX PAGE with no ant content at all. Needs a repoint to `ucanr_ext_ants` / `ucanr_ext_sooty_mold`, both already in the catalog. Same class as plum's San Jose scale citing a mealy plum aphid page (batch 17).

### One observation for the sweet-citrus batch, PRE-EXISTING and not introduced here

`release_verify` section G reports lemon's `calendar` as value-identical to orange-navel in 14 region cells. This promote did not author or touch a single calendar cell -- both crops' `regions` subtrees are byte-identical between base and candidate -- so this is pre-existing state surfaced by choosing a same-class reference, not collateral. It may well be legitimate (citrus in the cold zones is one container-and-overwinter story), but it should be looked at when sweet citrus is authored, since orange-navel is one of those three crops.

### On the harness finding nothing

Zero survivors on the FIRST sweep is not this project's usual result: the three promote suites built immediately before this one each had vacuous branches (three on batch 17, one on the mint). The difference here was method, not luck -- every driver was enumerated from the promote's own branch list rather than written to a description of what the guard was for, and each asserts the ONE message its branch emits, so a branch with no driver is visible while writing the suite instead of after running the harness. Two branches were reached only because of that enumeration: the closing SET assertion in `check_type_transition` (every per-problem mutation short-circuits past it, so it needed a driver that makes a pinned problem's pre-state type already fine) and the pair of `main()` catalog refusals, which the batch-17 shape of test could not reach at all.

Commits: batch 18 data + this state trio (one commit, since the pre-commit roster-claim check reads `LATEST.txt` from the INDEX) / register `514903db` in `COMMIT_FOR`. NOT PUSHED at time of writing; 3 prior commits also unpushed.

PLA-8 -- **MINT `ant_exclusion`, THE CATALOG'S 62nd METHOD** (`2a9d3c85` -> `2cde361b`; ONE promote; catalog 61 -> 62, source_catalog 215 -> 218, **ZERO crops touched**). **WHY: A DISEASE WHOSE ENTIRE CONTROL IS AN INSECT CONTROL.** Batch 18 (acid citrus) could not ship because `sooty-mold` is typed `fungal` while everything its record prescribes is INSECT control (suppress the honeydew producer, manage the ants that protect it, wash the film off); `TYPE_TARGETS` forbids a fungal type from naming any insect method, so lemon honestly emitted `control_ladder: null` rather than stretch a key, and `ladder_batch.py merge` CRASHES on that because the runner has no representation for a problem that cannot be laddered yet. Both citrus authors ALSO named ant exclusion the largest citrus gap independently, on scale and mealybugs whose own prose says "control ant access to the canopy (a sticky band on the trunk helps) so resident predators and parasites can work" -- playbook section 6: several bots blocked on the same control means the CATALOG. **THE FIRST ANCHOR CANDIDATE FAILED ON READING**: the URL the crops already cite for their ant advice, `ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/GARDEN/FRUIT/citrus.html`, is an INDEX PAGE with no ant content at all -- the exact `container_culture` failure the read-it-first rule exists to prevent, now FILED as a mis-pointed-key defect on lemon's mealybug and sooty-mold entries. Three T1 documents carry the claims: **Pest Notes 7411 (Ants)** for the mechanism ("the ants protect scales and aphids from their natural enemies") and the barrier plus its bark CAUTION (sticky material goes on a wrap, not bare bark); **Pest Management Guidelines: Citrus (Pub 3441)** for the citrus form (sticky "on top of a tree wrap", skirt prune 12 to 30 inches); and **Pest Notes 74108 (Sooty Mold)** as THE DISEASE-SIDE ANCHOR ("Control of sooty mold begins with managing the insect creating the honeydew"), which is the sole reason `disease_general` is in applies_to -- without it that half would be an INFERENCE across two steps and the mint would have left batch 18 blocked exactly as it was. **TIER IS `physical` AND THE MECHANISM AGREES WITH THE PRECEDENT**: every exclusion/barrier method in the catalog is physical, and the sources say exclude ants SO THAT natural enemies can work, so the rung must sort BELOW `beneficial_predators` -- physical < biological delivers that automatically, and a test asserts the ordering structurally rather than the string. **A54 CAUGHT THE FIRST CUT AND WAS RIGHT TO**: the source entries shipped `name` without `title` and gate_all went 121/121 FAILED. Titles were then READ OFF EACH DOCUMENT'S OWN `<title>`, never composed, and the promote now calls **A54's own checker** instead of re-implementing its rule -- which immediately exposed a second bug of mine, that `title_violations` takes the CATALOG dict and not `data`. Re-implementing would have hidden both. Suite **38/38**; **HARNESS 23/23, ZERO SURVIVORS** (24 anchors exactly once, positive control GREEN, sentinel RED), families blast/premise/scope/anchors/titles/hygiene/mechanics. ## 2026-08-28 -- PLA-8, THE `trap_cropping` CATALOG ROUND: a mint whose safety lives in its timing, and six refusals (`be444e25` -> `86c5396a` -> `96cbc68c`)

TWO promotes, the chlorothalonil pairing (`d096415` mint / `2e86279` backfill) applied again.
`tools/promote_pla8_trap_cropping.py` mints the key (catalog **58 -> 59**, zero crops, zero sources,
zero existing methods); `tools/promote_pla8_trap_cropping_backfill.py` attaches **10 rungs on 9
certified crops**, 20 register strings, zero catalog change. Roster laddered stays **46/121** because
these are rungs on ladders that already existed. Run in parallel with the main session's batches
11/12 under the SHA-collision protocol; this session took slot 1 by agreement.

**WHY IT WAS OWED.** Trap cropping is planting a sacrificial patch of a MORE preferred host to
concentrate a pest, then destroying that patch before it disperses. It was the single largest
unplaceable control in TWO CONSECUTIVE batches and all five batch-10 agents flagged it independently.
Every near-miss fails differently: `weed_host_control` REMOVES a host while this ADDS one;
`crop_rotation` moves the crop in space and `planting_time_avoidance` in time, while this leaves the
crop and changes what grows beside it; `garden_sanitation` covers the destroy step but not the
planting step; `beneficial_predators` attracts the pest's ENEMIES, this attracts the PEST.

**THE T1 READ ANCHORED THE TIMING, NOT THE PRACTICE.** A trap left standing is a nursery. UMass gave
the deadline ("must receive an insecticide application or be mechanically destroyed before eggs
hatch"), UF/IFAS the dispersal half ("you must eradicate them to prevent them from moving on to the
main crop") plus the harlequin-bug-on-collards case covering seven of the ten targets, UGA C1118 the
definition, two-weeks-early establishment and 8 to 12 ft separation. **TWO DOCUMENTS READ AND
DELIBERATELY NOT CITED:** Purdue's Vegetable Crops Hotline (right claim, but it lives on
vegcropshotline.org while `purdue_ext` is anchored at extension.purdue.edu -- the catalog-divergence
shape) and WVU's harlequin page, which carries the cleanest nursery warning of all and returned
**403 on both user agents**. A page that could not be read is not evidence, whatever a search summary
says about it.

**THE BRIEF WAS WRONG TWICE, AND BOTH WERE CAUGHT BY CHECKING RATHER THAN TRUSTING.** (1) It named
Clemson's cole-crop factsheet as carrying the harlequin trap-crop advice verbatim; fetched and read,
it says nothing about trap cropping. (2) Its scan reported 20 problems on 18 crops; re-run over EVERY
string field the true figure is **22 on 20**. `nasturtium`/Aphids and `zinnia`/Japanese beetles carry
their prose in `note_beginner`/`note_seasoned`, a shape used by **91 problems** on the shell and
ornamental crops and absent from the eight-field scan. Both are the INVERTED class and both are
textbook trap crops, so they are the records a later pass is most likely to get wrong. **The
exclusion set is SIX, not four.** The main session re-scanned independently, confirmed 22/20, and
corrected the brief in place.

**TWO RUNG CONTRACTS, ASSERTED IN CANONICAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** DESTROY_STATED (7 harlequin
entries) carry the removal step in their own prose, so their rungs restate it and attribute it with
"this crop's guidance". DIVERT_ONLY (3 flea-beetle entries) stop at the diversion and name no
endpoint, so their rungs route the timing through the METHOD's cautions and are FORBIDDEN the
attribution phrase -- crediting a source with a removal step it never states would author a
recommendation. That is batch 10's `planting_time_avoidance` ruling in a different field.

**THE SPECIES GUARD STOPS A PROPAGATION DEFECT.** The ten name different trap plants and jalapeno's
is NASTURTIUM, on a crop that is not a brassica. Every species a rung names is checked against THAT
CROP'S own prose. Exactly one pair is byte-identical (cabbage/cauliflower) and shares a rung text;
`check_rung_distinctness` pins the prose/rung correspondence in BOTH directions, catching a copied
rung and a needlessly forked one with the same check. Placement is the END OF THE CULTURAL RUN, not
the end of the ladder: all ten end above cultural, so appending would break monotonicity.

**SIX EXCLUSIONS, PINNED BOTH WAYS, EACH WITH ITS OWN REASON.** INVERTED (radish/flea-beetles,
nasturtium, zinnia), REPURPOSED (radish/cabbage-root-maggot), CONSERVATION (dill and parsley
parsleyworm, where larvae are relocated to KEEP THEM ALIVE on a host grown partly for the
butterflies, and a method meaning "then destroy the trap" is actively wrong rather than redundant).
**nasturtium is the most dangerous** and gets its own message: its text describes pulling a loaded
trap stand, which reads exactly like this method, but the dataset carries it as an ornamental and
edible crop, so a rung tells the reader to destroy the crop they are growing. Both promotes refuse if
any exclusion fails to RESOLVE to a real problem -- a typo'd slug would protect nothing while
reporting green.

**HARNESSES: 34/34 and 42/42, ZERO SURVIVORS, and run 1 of each found a REAL unreachable branch.**
The mint's per-exclusion branch was masked by the mint-only sweep; the backfill's "sits after a
non-cultural rung" check was structurally implied by monotonicity (cultural is the lowest rank) and
was DELETED rather than kept as decoration. **BOTH had been concealed by hedged-OR drivers** --
`assertTrue(a in out or b in out)` passes whether or not the branch under test can ever fire, which
makes it a smell rather than a convenience. A third ordering defect was fixed before the harness ran,
caught by `VerifyPostIsDriven` failing at first write: the verbatim check subsumes every substantive
check, so with it first the disclosure, contrast, applies_to and tier branches were all unreachable.

**A CLAIM MADE AND RETRACTED, recorded because it would have caused an audit.** This round first
reported that the `X or {...}` mutation idiom is inert wherever it appears, including in shipped
harnesses. **False.** `{} or {MANGLED FIRST KEY, ...rest}` renames a key, the guard's subscript
raises `KeyError`, and the suite reddens -- verified by evaluating both idioms directly, and the main
session's re-run of `mutate_pla8_chlorothalonil_backfill_suite.py` gives 30/30 PASS. Only `() or
(THE ORIGINAL PASTED BACK)` is truly inert. Shipped harnesses are SOUND; their labels are wrong.
Filed as a labeling cleanup, not an audit.

**GAUNTLET:** gate_all **121/121**; whole_crop_gate PASS on all nine; control_ladder_gate **0**;
register_completeness PASS; release_verify **clean** (only the nine declared crops changed,
`control_methods` the only top-level change, catalog +none -none, `lettuce-leaf` byte-identical);
COMPACT preserved; **134 guard tests green under both runners**. `release_verify` needed
`--slug cabbage`: its default pilot slug is `cherry-tomato`, which it folds into the expected-changed
set, so the default reports a spurious CONCERN. Known single-crop-pilot shape, not a finding.

Commits `70a2a9e` (mint), `fcb3ec7` (register `86c5396a`), `c64f8ed` (backfill), `1273c93` (register
`96cbc68c`). All `--no-verify` on the standing E1 sequencing; NOT pushed. Never amend the two that
COMMIT_FOR pins.

**OWED:** `brussels-sprouts`/Harlequin bug takes this rung in batch 12, whose promote now REFUSES to
ship without it; five more crops pick it up free when laddered (`blackberry`, `cayenne-pepper`,
`eggplant`, `habanero`, `okra`). WVU's 403 page is the best unclaimed anchor. **53 rungs across 5
crops carry no `note_seasoned` and `control_ladder_gate` never mentions the field** (broccoli 19/30,
celery 18/25, artichoke 8/30, asparagus 7/20, microgreens-mix 1/7) -- measured twice independently,
deliberately NOT gated mid-block, and owed a gate plus its own backfill after the fall block.

## 2026-08-24 -- PLA-8: the Bt safety absolute, and a mutation harness that failed first (afe4d697 -> 0f911326)

PLA-8 -- **THE BT SENTENCE WAS WRONG TWICE, AND THE SECOND HALF WAS THE WORSE ONE** (`afe4d697` -> `0f911326`; ONE promote; 9 `organic_treatment_beginner` strings on 9 crops -- kale, collards, spinach, arugula, bok-choy, cauliflower, cabbage, brussels-sprouts, kohlrabi; NO control_method, source, ladder, id, type or problem touched, no crop outside those nine). **THE DEFECT:** *"Spray Bt, which is safe and targets only caterpillars"*. **(1) "which is SAFE" is an unhedged absolute** -- NPIC (fetched and READ 2026-08-24) never uses "safe" without qualification: *"Bt is low in toxicity to people and other mammals when eaten"*, *"practically nontoxic and doesn't cause disease in birds, fish, and shrimp"*, EPA *"concluded that the Bt strains tenebrionis, israelensis, and kurstaki are low in toxicity to bees"*, and *"some pesticide products with Bt in them have caused eye and skin irritation"*. **(2) "targets ONLY caterpillars" is LITERALLY TRUE AND CONSUMER-MISLEADING, which is worse than a plain overstatement.** It reads as harmless to everything the gardener cares about, when **the non-target risk IS other caterpillars**: NPIC records that *"a few studies also found that non-target moths were harmed"*. A reader told Bt targets only caterpillars has been handed a reason to spray freely, which is the opposite of the intent. So the replacement carries BOTH halves -- the qualified toxicity claim and the non-target caveat -- and a refusal enforces each; either alone leaves the reader worse informed than a blank field. **THE CATALOG ALREADY HAD IT RIGHT, FOR THE THIRD TIME THIS ARC.** `control_methods.bt` carries *"Bt kurstaki kills the caterpillars of moths and butterflies as a group, including desirable species such as swallowtails and monarchs"* and *"it does not tell good caterpillars from bad"*. PLA-253 removed the absolute from the METHOD and **the remediation never reached the crops**. Check the catalog before assuming the whole record is wrong. **AND THE DATASET ALREADY KNEW THE NUANCE ON THREE OTHER CROPS**, which makes these nine inconsistent rather than merely unhedged: dill (*"rarely warranted on a host plant grown partly for the butterflies"*), viola (*"leaving native fritillary larvae where butterflies are wanted"*), parsley. All three untouched, and guarded as untouched. **READ, NOT COUNTED:** a Bt + safe/only/harmless scan returned 17 hits. NINE are this class. The other EIGHT are FALSE POSITIVES on four corn crops where "only" is about EFFICACY TIMING and is correctly stated (*"An organic Bt spray only works while they are still out on the leaves"*). Untouched, and a guard asserts both that they are unchanged AND that the sentences still exist, so the guard cannot go green by their vanishing. **THE HARNESS FAILED FIRST, WITH 3 SURVIVORS, AND FOUND TWO REAL GUARD WEAKNESSES.** (a) The source-read guard asserted *"low in toxicity"* appeared SOMEWHERE in the joined quotes; rewriting quote 1 to *"Bt is safe for people"* still left quote 3 qualified, so it passed for the wrong reason -- OVERLAP where it needed COVERAGE. Now every quote is checked individually and none may make a bare safety claim. (b) `REQUIRED_NONTARGET` weakened to `r""` matched everything and nothing noticed, because the constant was only ever validated against data the same module supplies. It now has negative and positive controls. (c) The third survivor was a BADLY-DESIGNED MUTATION, not a gap: disabling a refusal changes no output while the data still satisfies it; it was replaced with one that removes the caveat from the DATA. **Re-run: 17 injections, 17 CAUGHT, 0 survivors**, preflight 18/18, positive control GREEN, sentinel RED; six families -- safety 5, scope 3, coverage 2, blast 2, mechanics 3, record 2. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, recorded: the seasoned halves on four brassicas say Bt and spinosad *"target caterpillars and spare beneficials"* -- a DIFFERENT claim, true of non-Lepidopteran beneficials and incomplete about Lepidopteran ones, and folding it in would repeat scope creep this arc has twice resisted on purpose. GAUNTLET: suites **147/147**; gate_all **121/121**; control_ladder_gate 0; register_completeness PASS; release_verify clean; whole_crop_gate PASS on all nine touched crops; COMPACT preserved.

## 2026-08-23 -- PLA-8: water_at_the_base split (208e213c -> 75b3c0f0)

## 2026-08-23 -- PLA-8: two calcium-disorder methods (d19abe60 -> 208e213c)

PLA-8 -- **TWO NEW METHODS FOR CALCIUM-MOVEMENT DISORDERS, BECAUSE WIDENING THE OLD ONES WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THE WRONG PROSE** (`d19abe60` -> `208e213c`; ONE promote; `control_methods` 40 -> 42; NO crop touched, NO source minted, no existing method changed). **THE RULING (Trevor, 2026-08-23).** Blossom-end-rot controls were first proposed as `applies_to` widenings on `balance_nitrogen` and `straw_mulch`. Clemson HGIC's BER section supports the biology outright, and the widening was STILL WRONG: `applies_to` governs what the GATE accepts and does nothing to the PROSE a reader sees. `balance_nitrogen` says *"The soft, sappy new growth that too much nitrogen pushes out is exactly what aphids multiply on"* -- but BER's mechanism is ammonium COMPETING WITH CALCIUM UPTAKE, nothing to do with sappy growth or aphids. `straw_mulch` says *"A layer of straw around and between strawberry plants keeps the ripening berries up off the wet soil ... less likely to rot with gray mold"* -- a tomato BER ladder would have handed the reader strawberries and gray mold. Either widening would have let a bot author a rung that GATES CLEAN AND READS AS A NON-SEQUITUR, the same class as prose that passes every structural check and is still false. A method whose how_it_works must say "unless it is this other problem, in which case something else entirely" is TWO METHODS. **AND THEY DO NOT DUPLICATE `even_watering`**, which is already `physiological` and already states the calcium pathway: Clemson names two levers in one sentence, *"Maintain a uniform supply of moisture through irrigation AND adequate soil mulches"*. Watering is a schedule; mulch is a material laid once. Each new entry's `best_use` says explicitly which is which so an author cannot treat them as interchangeable. SOURCE (fetched and read 2026-08-23, `clemson_hgic` ALREADY catalogued T1 and already anchoring 5 methods, so nothing minted): *"The cause of this disorder is a calcium deficiency in the developing fruit"*; *"excessive ammoniacal (NH4+) nitrogen, potassium, or magnesium fertilization can also increase the chances of blossom end rot"*; *"Avoid ammoniacal nitrogen fertilizers for sidedress applications ... as ammoniacal nitrogen also will compete with calcium for uptake"*. `physiological` goes 5 -> 7 legal methods. **THE HARNESS'S DISTINCTNESS FAMILY IS THE POINT OF THE PROMOTE**, so it is the family most heavily mutated: drifting the nitrogen copy back to aphids, drifting the mulch copy back to strawberries, deleting either contrast sentence, and stripping the mulch mechanism -- **5 of 15 injections, all CAUGHT**. **A PREFLIGHT WAS ADDED AFTER THE HARNESS DIED THREE TIMES ON LINE-CONTINUATION ANCHORS:** a sentence that spans an implicit Python string concatenation is not a literal anywhere in the file, so the anchor matched 0x. Discovering that one mutation at a time wastes a suite run each time AND leaves a partial total on screen that reads like a result. Every anchor is now validated exactly-once BEFORE anything is graded; it caught two further bad anchors in one run. HARNESS: **15 injections, 15 CAUGHT, 0 survivors** across distinctness/scope/shape/sourcing/blast/refusal/mechanics, sentinel red, positive control green. GAUNTLET: suite 27/27; gate_all **121/121**; control_ladder_gate 0; register_completeness PASS; variety_ladder_delta 0; both prior PLA-8 promote suites still green; COMPACT preserved.
