## 2026-08-06 -- PLA-114 LEMON COLD ANCHOR: the promote whose own premise was refuted mid-session (6b2dcb8e -> 29b96b65, ONE promote)

**PLA-114 LEMON COLD ANCHOR** -- campaign D's lemon tail. `uc_anr_8100` minted (UC ANR 8100, *Frost Protection for Citrus and Other Subtropicals*), `lemon.frost_tolerance_f` 28 -> 29, nine bare citations repointed across four regions, five findings filed. >> THE PROMOTE'S OWN PREMISE WAS REFUTED MID-SESSION AND REBUILT. F1 and F5 were drafted on a scan reporting that lemon's "high-20s F" threshold appeared in 0 of the 17 readable documents it cites. That zero was the instrument: UF/IFAS HS1153/HS402, a lemon monograph this crop references 87 times and which was cached and readable throughout, publishes four lemon-specific figures (defoliation 22-24F, severe wood damage 20F, flowers and young fruit killed 29F, mature fruit damaged 28-31F). The scan required a temperature to be "lemon-adjacent" and the nearest "lemon" sits 333 characters away, because on a crop monograph the crop is the section's SUBJECT and the passage's own subject noun is "trees". Every proximity window from +/-60 to +/-300 returns a clean, confident zero. `tools/cited_claim_scan.py` is the regression: no proximity filter, uncached URLs reported UNDETERMINED, and `assert_absence_reportable` REFUSES to call a zero an absence when any cited URL is unread, when the readable set is empty, or when a proximity filter was used over a document whose title names the crop. >> A SECOND OVERSTATEMENT WAS CAUGHT AND REVERSED BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The corrected disposition first claimed the 14 strings asserting the threshold for leaves AND fruit were a stage conflation with the leaf half unsupported, and would have rewritten them. Wrong twice: HS402's 22-24F is DEFOLIATION, a severity ENDPOINT further along the same damage curve rather than a competing onset, and 8100's 29F covers foliage because it says PLANTS ("when temperatures fall to 29F for 30 minutes or longer, some frost damage to tender citrus plants will occur", under a "Trees" heading separate from its "Fruits" section). The axis is ONSET vs ENDPOINT, not leaves vs trees. Reading each string's clauses showed NONE asserts leaf death at the threshold -- all use damaged/injured, and every lethality clause is scoped to a different subject under a colder, separately-named condition. Counting lethality verbs per string flags 8 of 14; reading which noun each governs flags 0. **NO CONSUMER PROSE MOVED**, and all 14 strings are pinned byte-identical by path so a later pass cannot quietly "fix" correct copy. >> THIRD INSTANCE THIS CAMPAIGN of a mechanical proxy standing in for reading and returning a reproducible, confidently wrong answer (the proximity window, the `resolved_by_zone.3` path regex that reported SIBLING-PATHED = 0, and the verb count). Reproducibility is not validity. >> DELIBERATELY LEFT BARE because those hunts stay open: `se_gulf` z8 `clemson_hgic` (#28), `ca_interior` z8/z9 `ucanr_ext` (#3), and `warm_arid` plantings + plant_out (F3 -- hunt #31 covered 1 of its 3 nodes, not 3). >> `uc_anr_8100` records that its eScholarship URL is USER-AGENT GATED: a plain fetch returns HTTP 202, text/html, ZERO bytes, a success status carrying no document. >> GUARDS 46, RED before GREEN, 14 mutations all caught; TWO were vacuous on the first sweep and both failed the same way -- a substring that appears elsewhere (`'202'` matched the year 2026; satsuma/kumquat matched a different sentence of F5). >> GAUNTLET: whole_crop_gate lemon PASS, gate_all 121/121, release_verify no new concerns (the 16 novel-region-key CONCERNs are byte-identical on the base -- the known lettuce-leaf exemplar mismatch for tree crops), COMPACT preserved. ## 2026-08-05 (third pass) -- PLA-122 RULINGS: the precompute worry inverts, and turnip was a display bug (ca40d90f -> 6b2dcb8e, ONE promote)

Trevor's calls on campaign C's five open findings. 7 resolved cells edited, 1 provenance block added, 5 findings ruled. **This is the first promote in the campaign C sequence to MOVE CONSUMER-FACING STRINGS**, so the blanket "not one consumer string moves" tripwire the previous two leaned on is gone; it is replaced by an ENUMERATED before/after set with a guard proving nothing else inside those cells moved. 40 standalone roster gates byte-identical.

**THE PRECOMPUTE WORRY INVERTS, and measuring it first is the whole reason this landed cleanly.** PLA-122 flagged that these cells are `resolution_method: static_precompute` and warned that patching the resolved string leaves the upstream rule (`plant_out` from `last_frost`, `offset_days: 14`) able to regenerate Feb 1. It is the other way round. Both zones declare `last_frost: Jan 31` -- notably NOT `zone_frost_data`'s zone-10 Jan 15, since the region carries one anchor across both zones -- so the rule yields **Feb 14**, and **the rule never produced Feb 1**. The STORED value was the one that failed to reproduce, sitting 13 days off its own declared anchor. Trevor's Feb 15 lands within ONE day of the cell's own arithmetic, so AZ1005's first seed mark and the frost arithmetic are two independent lines arriving at the same date, and the edit makes these cells MORE reproducible rather than less. No offset needed reconciling. A guard now pins that relationship at plus or minus one day, and it is worth noting **that guard could not have been written before this edit**, because the pre-state failed it by thirteen days. Nothing re-runs the precompute over existing cells either, checked directly rather than assumed: `build_region_shells.py` reshapes key-sets idempotently and no-clobber, `build_mid_south_cells.py` is a one-off region build, and every other tool touching `offset_days` alongside `resolved_by_zone` is a one-off promote, a gate or a scan. `frost_anchor_reproduction_gate` reports 0 violations over 1,409 cells and cannot be tripped by this edit, since it fires only when two or more arm types agree on a DIFFERENT anchor.

**TURNIP WAS A DISPLAY RECONCILIATION, NOT A DATA CHANGE.** This was the check PLA-122 asked for and the answer is unambiguous: `first_plant_date` already read `Sep 1` and `last_plant_date` already read `May 31`, matching UC Master Gardeners San Diego ("Coastal: Seeds can be planted from September to May"). The sourced window was in the data all along and only the human-readable `plant_out` string was stuck at `Sep - Oct`. It now reads `Sep - May`, which is the wrap-around format **this crop's own `harvest` string already uses** (`Nov - May`). A guard asserts `first_plant_date` and `last_plant_date` do NOT move, which is what turns "display reconciliation" from a description into a checkable claim. CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the `calendar` array still marks Sep and Oct `plant` and Nov through May `harvest`. Those months are now both, a calendar cell carries ONE token per month, so the overlap cannot be expressed, and harvest is the more useful signal for a reader standing in January. That is the ribbon-granularity limit PLA-122 itself identified as an app-rendering question in the Code lane, recorded rather than papered over.

**THE OTHER THREE RULINGS.** watermelon's summer planting is DECLARED MODELED and kept, not dropped: AZ1005 marks low-desert watermelon at Feb 15, Mar 1 and Mar 15 and nothing else all year, which is a document actively indicating no second window rather than merely being silent about one, and that is stronger evidence than absence. Dropping it outright was offered and not taken; its two `second_planting` nodes stay on the institution root precisely because the document contradicts them. garlic keeps Apr 13, declared via a new `rgv` `plantings_provenance` block in the `{model, basis, supersedes}` shape its own thirteen other regions already use -- reverting would import a colder region's number, since Bexar County and our own se_gulf rows say May to June and the Rio Grande Valley is genuinely warmer than both. lavender is declared modeled: no university-published source gives a planting window for *Lavandula* in the desert Southwest, what exists is consumer and blog tier and not T1-admissible, and those non-citable sources converge on a range that brackets our existing window, so it is uncited rather than wrong. The two mislabelled source ids that finding also records need new catalog ids minted and are explicitly NOT in this patch.

**GUARDS: 15, EVERY ONE MUTATION-TESTED, AND FOUR WERE VACUOUS ON THE FIRST SWEEP.** Three were the same shape as the previous two promotes'. G6's permitted-ruling set was computed as `{fid for _s, fid in RULINGS}`, so it always contained whatever the promote changed; it is now the hand-written `RULED_IDS`, checked against `RULINGS` in both directions. G2 (only the enumerated fields moved) and G3 (melon harvest arms untouched) could not fail because the edit loop writes exactly the fields it then compares, so each earned a sabotage that actually reaches it -- a row declaring a no-op change for G2, a real harvest edit for G3. G7's footprint check needed `CROPS` shrunk before it could disagree with reality. **That is six instances of the computed-expected-value shape across three promotes in a single day**, every one found only by neutering the guard and watching the suite stay green.

**THE ISSUE'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT.** PLA-122 recorded that the `uscrn_validation` cross-check for the two melon rulings was unavailable because "all 22 hits per crop sit under rgv, pnw, mid_atlantic, mid_south, nevada, utah_dixie" and none under the desert regions, and inferred the desert regions lack USCRN coverage generally. The conclusion is right and the cause is not: cantaloupe and watermelon carry **zero** records, not 22 elsewhere, and the desert regions are not the gap at all (`warm_arid` 16, `low_desert_az` 8, `ca_desert` 8, of 220 records over 38 of 128 crops). **All 220 records sit on `direct_sow` arms**, which is PLA-110's deliberate scope, and the three melons model **every one of their 17 regions as `plant_out`**, so they carry no `direct_sow` arm anywhere and are structurally outside USCRN's reach. No amount of desert backfill would have supplied the tiebreaker. The interesting residue is the modeling mismatch this exposes: AZ1005 marks both melon rows **S, its token for seeds**, and the RGV guides likewise treat melons as sown, while our data models them as transplants everywhere. For a direct-sown cucurbit soil temperature is the governing anchor, so these are exactly the crops the USCRN table was built for, and the `plant_out` modeling is what puts them out of reach. Worth measuring roster-wide.

**GAUNTLET.** `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all 5 touched crops, `gate_all` 121/121, `release_verify` "no new violations" with `catalog +none -none` and its user-facing dash and spelled-degrees scan clean (which matters here, since this promote moves consumer strings), 40 standalone gates byte-identical, COMPACT preserved.

## 2026-08-05 (second pass) -- AZ1005, THE DIVERGENCE SCAN, AND LAVENDER: two of three recommendations were wrong once the documents were read (754c51a0 -> ca40d90f, ONE promote)

The three follow-ups campaign C left open, each with a recommendation attached. Reading the documents overturned two of them, which is the argument for reading them. Citations and findings only: 20 nodes repoint, 3 stay bare by design, 6 findings filed, no catalog id minted, 40 standalone roster gates byte-identical.

**AZ1005 WAS A REPOINT, NOT AN ABSENCE.** The closeout deliberately filed no absence finding for cantaloupe, honeydew-melon and watermelon on the grounds that AZ1005 was a live lead rather than a measured absence. That call is vindicated twice: the document HAS both melon rows, so an absence finding would have been false, and it does NOT support every window we publish, so a blanket repoint would have been false too. Its text layer holds crop names and no dates, so the grid was reconstructed from CHARACTER COORDINATES -- month labels share an x and vary in y, which confirms the documented 90-degree rotation mechanically instead of assuming it -- and the method was VALIDATED AGAINST A CONTROL before any melon was touched: pumpkin reads Mar 1, Mar 15, then Jul 1, Jul 15, Aug 1 off the grid, and our pumpkin cell says plant_out Mar 1 - Mar 15 with a second planting Jul 1 - Jul 31. Reproducing a value we already hold is what makes the rest of the reading trustworthy.

The two rows disagree with each other, and that is the finding. "Melons, Cantaloupe Honeydews, etc." carries S marks from Feb 15 continuously through Jul 15. "Melons, Watermelon" carries S at Feb 15, Mar 1 and Mar 15 and **nothing else all year**. So the verdicts split three ways rather than being one blanket: honeydew opens Feb 15 against a document that opens Feb 15, clean, all five nodes repoint; cantaloupe opens Feb 1, a fortnight ahead of the first mark, and runs to Aug 15 where the document stops at Jul 15, so it is repointed with the divergence filed open; and watermelon's Jul 15 - Aug 15 second planting has no support at all, so its three spring nodes repoint and its **two second_planting nodes stay bare** with a filed reason. The asymmetry is evidence rather than a gap in the table: the same document gives cantaloupe and honeydew five months and gives watermelon six weeks, which is a real horticultural claim about a longer-season crop in a hot desert. Recorded separately, because it will otherwise be misread later: honeydew has no row of its OWN. It rides the combined cantaloupe row, so the document cannot distinguish the two crops' timing and does not independently confirm that honeydew should open later than cantaloupe. Neither early opening is called an error -- Maricopa County is one part of a larger region, and a fortnight at the front of a direct-sown cucurbit window is where soil temperature governs rather than the calendar -- but neither is sourced, and the early end is the one that costs a reader a planting, since seed into cold February soil rots.

**THE DIVERGENCE SCAN SHIPS NARROW, AND THE FOUR REJECTED WIDENINGS ARE PINNED BY A TEST.** `tools/catalog_divergence_scan.py` reports the one definition that does not flood: the node cites a domain ROOT while that source id's catalog entry already names a DOCUMENT. Eight nodes, two ids. `bare_host_scan` cannot see the class because it never consults `source_catalog`, and `url_health_gate` cannot because every one returns HTTP 200. Measured the same day and all flooding: by-domain comparison, 729 nodes, where `cameron.agrilife.org`, `aggie-horticulture.tamu.edu`, `fieldreport.caes.uga.edu` and `nevegetable.org` are all legitimate; one-id-carrying-many-documents, 47 ids, with `ncsu_ext` alone spanning 83 urls of which 51 are off-host and essentially all correct; catalog-names-a-pathed-document-but-node-cites-another, which flags the ASPCA toxic-plant index and its per-plant pages, a correct arrangement; and that last one with descendants and same-host pages excluded, which still floods because "pathed" is not "specific document" -- `msu_bozeman`'s catalog url is `montana.edu/extension/`, a portal that happens to have a path. A test pins those numbers so the next reader does not see eight rows, conclude the scan is timid, and rediscover the flood.

**THE OBVIOUS TURNIP TARGET WAS A DEAD LINK.** Turnip's seven `ca_south_coast` nodes cited the San Diego Master Gardeners bare root while eight sibling crops cited per-crop pages on that same host. The url shape those siblings use is plural (`/beets/`), and `/turnips/` returns HTTP 404. The real page is `/turnip/`, singular. Pattern-matching a sibling's url would have installed a dead link, which is the sibling-precedent trap in its cheapest possible form and the reason that trap is worth re-reading before every repoint. What the page says is also WIDER than what we publish: seeds from September to May coastal and September to April inland, against our Sep - Oct. Our window is a conservative subset, so nothing is wrong and no date moved, but a reader is being shown a shorter season than the source we now cite; filed for a content pass. edamame's one node stays bare because no Cornell edamame VARIETY document exists: the gardener-facing Vegetable Varieties database requires authentication, the only Cornell edamame publication is a 2014 Expo proceedings PDF, and the CALS soybean varieties page covers agronomic soybean by maturity group, a different use of the same species.

**A REGISTRABLE-DOMAIN MATCH IS THE WRONG INSTITUTION TEST**, found when this promote's own first guard rejected the turnip repoint. `ucanr_san_diego_mg`'s catalog url sits on `ucanr.edu` while the county association runs `mastergardenersd.org`. County Master Gardener programs routinely run a separate `.org` beside their university program page, so a domain comparison rejects correct citations. The guard now requires the host to be already vouched for by OTHER crops under that exact id, which is looser on domain and stricter in substance.

**LAVENDER WAS NOT A RELABEL.** It was queued as cosmetic, an id pointing at the wrong document. Reading all three of its NMSU sources shows that NONE of them publishes a lavender planting date. Guide H-221 gives seed-germination guidance only. RR-770 is a cultivar trial for NORTH-CENTRAL New Mexico -- the wrong half of the state for a warm_arid cell -- whose only date is when the trial plot was established in June 2002. The low-water plants list covers the right taxon, *Lavandula angustifolia*, and gives water need, height and sun exposure with no planting time and no zone. So the plant_out window is modeled and says so nowhere, and two of the three citations are additionally mislabelled, which is how it stayed invisible. **No scan in the repo can reach this**: the node is neither bare nor sole, so both scans pass it, and every mechanical widening of the divergence check floods.

**GUARDS: 12, EVERY ONE MUTATION-TESTED, AND THREE WERE VACUOUS ON THE FIRST SWEEP -- ALL THE SAME SHAPE.** `AZ1005_URL` was read out of the catalog and then compared against the catalog, which cannot fail; it is now a pinned constant asserted in both directions. The turnip host-vouching set was computed over the whole pre-state, so turnip's own seven bare citations put `mastergardenersd.org` into the set and licensed their own replacement; it is now computed from other crops only. And one test stripped turnip's own citation, tripping `PREFLIGHT 1` rather than the guard it named, caught only because these tests assert the specific abort message. Three in this promote after two in the previous one is a consistent enough pattern to state as a rule: **when a guard's expected value is COMPUTED rather than written down, assume it is vacuous until a mutation proves otherwise.**

**GAUNTLET.** `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all 6 touched crops, `gate_all` 121/121, `release_verify` "no new violations" with `catalog +none -none` on every crop, 40 standalone gates byte-identical, COMPACT preserved.

Measured roster-wide over 29,390 anchoring entries: comparing node urls to catalog urls **by domain floods at 729**, nearly all legitimate multi-domain institutions such as `cameron.agrilife.org`, `txmg.org` and `nevegetable.org`; narrowed to **"node is BARE while the catalog knows a PATHED document" it yields exactly 10 nodes over 3 ids** -- carrot's 2, seven turnip nodes under `ucanr_san_diego_mg`, and one edamame node. `bare_host_scan` cannot see this because it never consults `source_catalog`, and `url_health_gate` cannot because every one of them returns HTTP 200. Narrow the CHECK, not its scope.

**HUNTS 17 AND 24 CLOSED ON ONE CHART, AND IT HAD TO BE READ AS AN IMAGE.** Both tomatoes' `basis_seasoned` names its document in prose -- "Dona Ana County Master Gardener Las Cruces planting chart" -- which is precisely what `nmsu_chart` points at, so one read served both hunts. That chart's planting windows are drawn as GRAPHICAL BARS: its text layer holds crop names, month headers and zero dates. This is the AZ1005 rotated-grid trap in a second document, and here it does not yield a wrong grid, it yields an empty one, which is the more dangerous failure because a text extraction returns something that looks like a clean parse. Read visually instead: carrots mid-January through February with a second bar August into early September; tomatoes transplanting March into early April, then mid-July into early August. Both match the cells exactly.

**GUARDS: 13, EVERY ONE MUTATION-TESTED, AND TWO WERE WRONG ON THE FIRST SWEEP.** G4, which re-checks the held nodes after the edits, passed all 26 tests when neutered -- decoration by this arc's own rule. It earned a test instead of being deleted, because it is the only guard that can catch a path added to REPOINTS while still sitting in HELD, and PREFLIGHT2 cannot cover that since it runs before the edits. Worse, G8's expected sets were DERIVED from the very tables they validated, which is the `guard-derived-from-what-it-checks-is-vacuous` shape reproduced in my own code; they are now hand-written constants checked in both directions, against the data and against the tables. A test also failed for the right reason and was itself wrong: it expected an abort when `nmsu_chart`'s catalog url was moved to `pubs.nmsu.edu`, and the promote correctly allowed it, because carrot already cites the chart PDF under that id on its `direct_sow` arms. The three vouching rules each turn out to be load-bearing for exactly one repoint, and the promote asserts all three are exercised.

## 2026-08-04 -- USCRN SOIL-TEMPERATURE VALIDATION LANDS (4065e23b -> 5a52a76c, ONE promote, UNCOMMITTED pending Trevor)

PLA-110. Two writes, and guards prove nothing else moved: 14 standalone roster gates are byte-identical between the pre-promote base and the result.

**WHAT LANDED.** (1) A new top-level `uscrn_soil_temp`, sibling of `zone_frost_data`: for each USDA zone and each of 12 thresholds, the measured distribution of the date 5cm soil temperature first holds that threshold for 5 consecutive days, over 2010-2025, from all 113 NOAA USCRN stations and 1,802 station-years. This is the durable asset. It is measurement the project owns rather than another extension table, and it is the half of the pass that does not depend on the threshold question below. The 50F gradient comes out monotonic across zones, as it must: z3 05-11, z4 05-09, z5 04-27, z6 04-15, z7 03-12, z8 02-02, z9 01-06, z10 01-01, on 72 to 330 station-years each. (2) 228 `uscrn_validation` records on direct-sow cells.

**THE ISSUE'S FRAMING WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS, and all three were re-verified against the data before any code.** First, the "9 of 3,403 slots" denominator is off by a factor of eight. Two thirds of those slots cannot be soil-validated even in principle: 1,940 sit on `harvest_start`/`harvest_end`, where timing follows days-to-maturity from planting, and 326 sit on `start_indoors`, which happens in a heated house in a tray. The field's real universe is `direct_sow`: 425 slots, 408 joinable. The pilot's 9 was 2 percent of the target, not 0.3 percent. Second, "complete or re-run that integration" had nothing to re-run; no USCRN puller, validator or integration existed anywhere in `tools/`. Third, and most important, the 9-record pilot was not a safe template to copy. **bok-choy / northern_tier was byte-identical to lettuce-leaf / northern_tier** -- same `stored_date` 03-18, same median, same 14 stations, same 198 station-years -- for a crop that stores no Mar 18 date in any zone (its z6 is Mar 22, its z7 Mar 1). All nine were retired and rebuilt.

**A CORRECTION TO THAT FINDING, made by re-reading the data rather than the inference.** The first write-up said bok-choy's 40F threshold was also lettuce's number leaking across. It is not. The 40F anchor is declared on bok-choy's own planting arm and sourced to bok-choy's own MSU Extension prose ("bok choy ... germinates once soil reaches about 40 degrees F"), so it legitimately overrides the 45F optimal-band floor. What was copied was the record PAYLOAD, the date and the station counts, not the threshold. A guard that had been written to demand 45F there was asserting an inference against the evidence, and was replaced by one that re-derives every record's `stored_date` from its own cell.

**TWO VERDICT METHODS WERE BUILT, MEASURED ON THE REAL ROSTER, AND REJECTED.** Recorded here so they are not rebuilt. The Phase 1.1 fixed-day bands named in the issue (within 3 days aligned, 4 to 10 drift, beyond 10 misaligned) returned **170 of 228 cells "misaligned"**, including 16 of the 29 whose arm declares its own soil anchor. That is not a roster full of defects: a zone's own crossing swings 30 to 90 days between p10 and p90, so a 3-day band is finer than the quantity it measures and reports variance as error. Those bands were specified for a comparison against a single station, not a zone aggregate. They are retained as a reported `offset_band` but are not the verdict. The second attempt compared the sowing window's OPENING date against the median crossing and returned 67 cells "often too cold"; a sowing window is a range a gardener picks a day inside, so its opening precedes the typical crossing by construction. What survived compares the whole WINDOW against the measured distribution -- `window_too_early`, `opens_early`, `brackets_crossing`, `opens_late`, `not_soil_limited` -- giving 167 / 12 / 3 / 45 / 1 and 28 cells carrying directional risk. A readable review surface instead of a flood.

**TREVOR'S TWO RULINGS.** Threshold basis: ship on the OPTIMAL `germination_temp_f` floor, with `anchor_threshold_basis` naming that provenance on every record, and a guard pinning it so the ruling cannot quietly erode. This is explicitly not the finish line. `germination_temp_f` is an optimal band and not a germination minimum -- `docs/climate_thresholds_contract.md` says so outright, and cucumber reads 70F against a true minimum near 60F -- which flips verdicts on identical data: the six utah_dixie cucurbit cells sit 45 days ahead of the measured crossing at 70F, but at 60F the same zone's median is 03-23 against a stored 03-15, which is fine. PLA-118 carries the real germination-minimum field, and **no app-facing USCRN-validation claim rests on this pass**. Register row: NOT added, deliberately. The field is meaningful on 408 of 6,579 date entries and on zero entries for all 31 tree, berry and mushroom crops, none of which is ever seed-sown, so an A39 presence-or-null requirement would tax every future fruit-tree certification for nothing. `tools/uscrn_coverage_scan.py` replaces it as a soft scan in the shape of `soil_temp_floor_scan.py`, and reports **0 unexplained gaps**: 532 cell-zones covered, 89 fall-only, 59 in zones 11-13 where USCRN has no station at all.

**METHOD DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING.** Station-to-zone needed no external data: a USDA zone IS the mean annual extreme minimum temperature binned in 10F steps from -60F, and USCRN publishes daily minima, so each station is binned from its own record. All 113 resolved, 0 dropped, spot-checked against published placements (Fairhope AL 9a, Batesville AR 7a, Tucson AZ 9b). A year only scores if it contains its own winter, because a station that lost January reports a falsely warm minimum and walks a zone south. Records are keyed to the CELL, not to an arm index: arms align positionally with resolved window segments only 51 percent of the time here. A missing daily reading breaks the 5-day sustain run rather than being interpolated, and an unwatched year is never counted as "the soil never got there". Feb 29 folds to Feb 28, because the dataset stores month-day strings and an emitted 02-29 is a date that does not exist three years in four. Warm-zone saturation is flagged rather than reported as a spring event: zone 8 is already at or above 40F on Jan 1 in 67 percent of years, zone 9 in 79 percent.

**GUARDS: 8, and ONE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED.** A "no two crops share an identical record" check looked like the right fingerprint for the pilot's copy defect and is not: six cucurbits legitimately produce byte-identical utah_dixie records (same 70F floor, same window, same zone), the first version compared whole germination bands and false-positived on a 90-vs-95 upper bound, and once corrected it could not fail at all because two earlier guards already covered it. Removed rather than shipped, with the reasoning left in place. Separately, guard ORDER was corrected: the slot-count check was unreachable behind the structural comparison, so its mutation test was passing only because an earlier guard fired -- the `guard-tests-pass-because-an-earlier-check-fires` shape, hit again. 84 tests across five suites, every guard mutation-tested.

**A29 CAUGHT A REAL MISTAKE MID-PASS.** The records first used the pilot's `zone_coverage_note_seasoned`. The `_seasoned` suffix is a CONTRACT, not a label: `register_fill_gate` requires every `_seasoned`/`_beginner` field to be authored prose with a register twin, and it bounced **34 of 121 certified crops** until the field was renamed to `zone_coverage_note`. These are machine-generated methodology annotations on a field that renders nowhere, not the expert half of a dual-register consumer pair.

**GAUNTLET.** `gate_all` 121/121, `whole_crop_gate` PASS, `release_verify` clean (its 4 review notes are pre-existing Step 5/5.5 items), 14 standalone roster gates byte-identical to the base, compact preserved, no trailing newline. UNCOMMITTED, awaiting Trevor; on commit register `5a52a76c` -> <commit> in `promote_fixture.COMMIT_FOR`. No plant-astro bump. Evidence: `docs/2026-08-04-uscrn-soil-temp-validation-arc.md`.

## 2026-08-04 -- TREVOR'S RULINGS: CAMPAIGN B'S 7 OPEN DECISIONS CLOSED (47a502af -> 4065e23b, ONE promote, UNCOMMITTED pending Trevor)

Consumer prose and finding status ONLY. 8 finding records ruled, 6 strings rewritten, 1 new finding filed. Guards assert separately that no suitability value, date, calendar, planting or citation moved anywhere, because the entire ruling turned on RETAINING those values. Campaign B now carries exactly ONE open finding, and that one is open deliberately.

**cherry-sweet's NC State credit: RESTATE, NOT DELETE.** The cell told readers in both registers that NC State "steers zone 8 growers toward sour cherry instead, which tolerates this humidity far better". It now credits only what NC State publishes (sour cherry is the hardier of the two, and is self fertile while sweet cherry needs a second variety) and moves the humidity claim OUTSIDE the attribution as our own read. That is exactly the shape cherry-sour's own zone 8 cell already used, so the siblings stop contradicting each other. Deletion was rejected because NC State does support two real advantages and the steer toward sour cherry genuinely helps a reader; what was wrong was the zone-8 SCOPE and the humidity RATIONALE, not the recommendation.

**strawberry z8 plant_out: KEEP Sep 15 - Oct 5, put the gradient in the copy. Trevor reversed the proposed trim, and was right to.** The reasoning is worth preserving because it generalizes. The mechanism UAEX describes is CONTINUOUS, not a threshold: fewer days before dormancy give fewer branch crowns, hence fewer flowers, hence less fruit. No source claims a survival risk. For a home bed, 15 to 35 percent is a couple of quarts, not a lost season. And the trim carried the WORSE failure mode: UAEX's own article notes growers must delay when ground is too wet and that fall hurricanes push wet weather up from the Gulf, so a gardener who cannot plant until October 2 would read a September 30 cutoff, conclude the window had closed, and possibly not plant at all -- trading a lighter crop for NO crop. UAEX never says do not plant in October; it says every week of delay costs yield, which is advice to plant EARLY, not a deadline. The real defect was never the tail: it was that a flat date range presents September 20 and October 3 as equivalent when UAEX measured that they are not. Fixed where a reader will see it.

**apricot and cherry coastal-plain suitability: RECORDED, NOT ACTIONED. `marginal` RETAINED on all three cells. The research came in AGAINST the tightening I proposed.** Cross-region calibration settled it: apricot is `marginal` in se_gulf zones 8, 9 and 10, which are HOTTER and MORE humid than the mid_atlantic Coastal Plain, so flipping this cell to `unsuitable` would assert apricot does better on the Gulf Coast than in Virginia and North Carolina, which is backwards. In every other hot-humid region apricot is `survives_no_fruit`, never `unsuitable`. The cherries are weaker still: the Plant Toolbox gives both Prunus cerasus and Prunus avium as 3a-8b, so zone 8 sits INSIDE NC State's published range, and the only evidence pushing against is one Pender County sentence lumping cherries, bunch grapes, raspberries and apricots under a single reason -- the shape that repeatedly turns out partly wrong when split by crop. What the evidence DID justify was PROSE: apricot's zone 8 note now tells the reader NC State places the crop in the Mountains and Piedmont, zones 5a to 7b, rather than the Coastal Plain, and that its Pender County office reports trees there are hard to keep alive beyond a few years.

**Three declared modeled** (apricot harvest divergence, pomegranate bloom window, elderberry planting model), each on one principle: DO NOT SWAP ONE UNSOURCED MODEL FOR ANOTHER, which is the call Trevor made on strawberry's bloom offset on 2026-08-03. Apricot's "late June to July" is a species-level Toolbox line with no regional table behind it, and retuning harvest would force changing an unsourced bloom offset too. Pomegranate's source describes an ORNAMENTAL long-bloom habit while our field models the fruit-setting bloom the harvest derives from; taking it literally would render a bloom band covering most of the year. Elderberry's "midsummer" is a season word in a garden column, weaker than the model it would overturn, and that crop has never had a gold-standard pass.

**THE FIND, caught while writing the strawberry edit: A SECOND, STILL-LIVE INSTANCE OF A KNOWN FABRICATED CREDIT.** `grown_as_note_seasoned` called plasticulture the system "the University of Arkansas recommends" when FSA6103 says it "is not recommended for home garden strawberry production at this time". The 2026-08-03 pass found and corrected that exact claim in `plantings_provenance` and never reached this field. The distinction that matters and that the finding records: **`plantings_provenance` RENDERS NOWHERE, while `grown_as_note_seasoned` RENDERS TODAY** in BerryYearCalendarCard.astro. So the pass corrected the invisible copy and left the visible copy asserting the opposite of the source. Removed subtractively per the herb-pass precedent (the credit goes, the horticultural fact stays). Lesson filed: correct EVERY field carrying an attribution, and check the RENDERING ones first.

**All six rewritten strings went into fields VERIFIED to render before writing** -- `suitability_note_seasoned`/`_beginner` are read by HardinessFruitingCard.astro and `grown_as_note_seasoned`/`_beginner` by BerryYearCalendarCard.astro. Checked in plant-astro first, per the lesson that a note in an unrendered field informs nobody.

**STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY: `strawberry_mid_south_plasticulture_home_garden_tension`.** Two T1 documents from one institution genuinely disagree about whether the annual system belongs in a home garden, and neither is wrong. Now that the false credit is gone from the copy, the remaining question is purely whether to present the system at all, which is Trevor's to rule. **A guard PINS it open** so a later pass cannot quietly close it as tidy-up.

**GUARDS: 20, ALL LOAD-BEARING** (25 tests, green under pytest AND the direct runner). One was vacuous on the first mutation sweep -- the top-level footprint check, whose test I had omitted -- and was fixed by adding the test rather than deleting the guard. Two probe strings had to be rewritten because the kept-facts check fired first and masked the guard under test, which is the 'an earlier check catches the sabotage' trap in miniature.

**GAUNTLET:** whole_crop_gate PASS on all 6 crops; gate_all 121/121; the 8 standalone gates BYTE-IDENTICAL to the session-start capture; release_verify "no new violations introduced" with its user-facing dash and spelled-degrees scan clean, its single CONCERN being the expected 6-crop footprint. COMPACT preserved, no trailing newline.

**CAMPAIGN B IS COMPLETE**: documents closed 2026-08-04 earlier in the day, decisions ruled here. Next campaign C (arid + Texas, 7 hunts) and campaign D (the tail, 11 hunts but 7 of them lemon -- invert the unit and read lemon's citations end to end). RE-PRICE BOTH BEFORE HUNTING. THE REASON: NC State's stated advantages for sour cherry are COLD HARDINESS and SELF-POLLINATION (Toolbox: "much more cold hardy than sweet cherry trees and is self-pollinating"; Henderson County: self-fertile vs needing two varieties). Humidity tolerance is ours. The tell is the sibling cell: `cherry-sour`'s own zone 8 prose attributes the hardiness and self-fertility facts to NC State and leaves the humidity sentence UNATTRIBUTED -- same content, and cherry-sweet's version moved the claim INSIDE the attribution and added a zone-8 scope. It is consumer copy in both registers, so the rewrite is Trevor's ruling, not a sourcing fix.

## 2026-08-03 (desert July note) -- the midsummer sowing explained in the reader's copy (`3f6d6ce4` -> `3b7dc544`)

**Prose only, and an EDIT to prose that already existed.** 8 strings = 4 crops (acorn / butternut / spaghetti squash, pumpkin) x `ca_desert` x both registers. No field added, no value moved, no citation moved, no finding filed.

**THE CORRECTION THAT MADE THIS POSSIBLE, and it was a correction of my own reasoning.** I had told Trevor this note was *blocked* on the frontend. It was not, and the framing was wrong twice over:

1. **`region_notes_seasoned` / `region_notes_beginner` ALREADY EXIST and are already populated** -- measured 2026-08-03: **1,808 of 1,878 region cells**, and the only 70 gaps are **exactly the 7 uncertified shells x 10 regions** (avocado, olive, and the 5 mushrooms). So **all 121 certified crops carry both registers in every region they have**, with **zero** cells holding a beginner note without a seasoned one (`release_verify` section F already enforces that pairing). It is **not a schema change and not a cross-crop field addition** -- no register entry, no A39-style presence gate, no backfill treadmill. The only outstanding work is wiring plant-astro, which is a frontend task in the astro session's lane.
2. **"Ship the frontend first" does not apply here.** [[fail-open-renderer-hides-new-values]] guards against a consumer **failing OPEN on an unknown value**, turning a data improvement into a regression. Nothing reads this field, so editing it cannot regress anything -- the copy simply sits correct and waiting until the renderer lands. Over-applying that rule is what produced the false "blocked" call.

**WHAT THE COPY DOES AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SAY.** These cells already stated that a midsummer sowing happens around July; they never said **why**, and the timing reads as a mistake to anyone who knows an Imperial Valley July. The added sentences say the July timing is deliberate because it places flowering and fruit set in the milder weather of early fall. **They state NO temperature and NO fruit-set threshold.** Cucurbit pollen viability does collapse somewhere in the low 90s °F, but that was **not sourced this session**, and writing a number the record cannot support is [[fill-the-shape-is-the-defect]]. The qualitative claim is a restatement of the crop's own calendar (sow July, harvest Oct 1 - Nov 1), not a new assertion. A guard **refuses any digit-plus-degrees pattern** in the rewritten copy, and another refuses any institution name, because these `ca_desert` arms are the 8 decisions HELD on `ca_desert_fall_cycle_provenance_gap` and still cite a bare host.

**GUARDS: 14, all mutation-tested, and the 2 that came back vacuous were made REACHABLE rather than deleted** -- unlike the two unfailable checks removed earlier today, each of these guards a real scenario. The duplicate-sentence guard was invisible because the pinned-tail guard fires first on a re-run *appended after* the tail; it becomes reachable when the sentence is inserted **before** the tail, which the tail guard cannot see. The whitespace-artifact guard needed a shim emitting a doubled space. Suite **20/20 both runners**; re-run **14/14 real, 0 vacuous**.

**GAUNTLET.** `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all 4; `gate_all` **121/121**; all 5 standalone gates exit 0 **and byte-identical to the pre-state capture**; `release_verify` differs from an unchanged-baseline run by **exactly one line** (the crops-changed CONCERN naming exactly the 4) with *"no new violations introduced"*; COMPACT preserved. `3f6d6ce4` registered in `promote_fixture.CHAIN`.

**TREVOR'S COMMUNITY-TIPS RULING, recorded because it shapes the frontend work:** one plant suggestion first, then community suggestions in a **separate slot below it**, never merged into the authored note. **Every submission is sent to plant, verified, and only then added** -- nothing auto-posts. That moderation model simplifies the provenance design: verified tips are authored content with a community *origin*, so what is needed is an origin/attribution field, not a trust-weighting model. Region-scoped to start; county or ZIP can be added later if user volume justifies it, and `resolved_by_zone` already exists as the finer slot.

## 2026-08-03 (campaign A closeout) -- 5 CASE 2 findings, three different reasons, one caught by a guard (`e65aa63a` -> `3f6d6ce4`)

**Findings only: not one citation, window or prose byte moved.** 5 findings / 5 crops / 9 decisions. **The scan stays at 115 decisions, and that is correct** -- a CASE 2 ruling leaves the bare host in place by design, which is precisely what the hunt ledger exists to record. **Genuinely open is now 91.**

**THE CLOSEOUT NEEDED THREE DIFFERENT REASONS, AND A GUARD CAUGHT ME BLANKETING ONE ACROSS ALL FIVE.** This is `never-blanket-a-reason-across-crops` firing again, and it would have written a false statement into canonical:

- **No row in the table** (accepted) -- `arugula`, which the table simply lacks, and `edamame`, whose only candidate row is *"beans, snap"*: **Phaseolus vulgaris, not Glycine max**. Matching that row on the word "beans" is the match-the-taxon trap.
- **The row exists but carries no regional resolution** (accepted) -- **`okra`, which needs the OPPOSITE ruling from the crops the table omits.** Okra *is* in the table, and its row reads `May` / `April-May` / `May` / `May`. Three of four regions are one month, and the two it treats **identically** are Monterey County north and the Imperial Valley: the coldest and the hottest summer climates in California. A row that cannot separate those cannot adjudicate a per-region window, so our `ca_desert` March opening and `ca_north_coast` z9 June opening are not contradicted by it, they are **not addressed** by it. The page says as much: *"planting dates are only approximate, as the climate may vary even in small sections of the state."* **No date changed** -- trimming a per-region window to a state-wide single month would destroy real regional information.
- **Cites the wrong root entirely** (open) -- **the pears, and this is the catch.** `pear-asian` and `pear-european` do **not** cite the vegetable table at all. They cite `https://homeorchard.ucanr.edu/`, the **UC Home Orchard** root, which is the *right class* of document for a pear and is missing only its specific page. The drafted "the vegetable table has no tree fruit row" text would have **asserted something false about their citation**. A preflight guard pinning the exact bare URL **per decision**, rather than reading it from a global bare-host map, aborted the promote and forced the correction. They are filed **`status: open`** as CASE 1 repoint candidates, deferred to the UC fruit-tree read that also owes their `ca_north_coast`/`ucanr_marin_mg` decisions -- the same two crops, so one pass settles both -- with an explicit note that *Pyrus pyrifolia* and *Pyrus communis* must be checked separately against whichever page is located.

`lemon` (4) and `lime` (3) were deliberately left out: same no-row shape, but they belong to campaign D's lemon cluster where one crop-centric read serves seven hunts at once. Filing them here would do the work twice.

**MUTATION TESTING CAME BACK 12/12 REAL ON THE FIRST TRY**, by applying the repoint promote's lesson from earlier the same day. One guard of my own -- a separate top-level-key check -- was proven unreachable (the `stripped()` whole-document compare already covers it) and was **removed rather than left standing as decoration**.

**TREVOR'S RULINGS THIS SESSION.** Keep the July desert second planting. Leave all 8 cucurbit decisions blocked by the fall-cycle gap rather than repoint at node granularity. **On the fall gap itself:** it is not a hole in our data -- the cycle is there and is horticulturally sound -- it is a hole in the *California literature*. UC gives pumpkins `March-June` with no fall cycle at all, and for winter squash publishes **August** where we say July. Recorded for a future arc: the discriminating question is **not** "is it too hot to survive" (July and August differ by roughly a degree in the low desert, and both sit far above our own `germination_temp_f` ceiling of 95 °F, so that test condemns both dates and must therefore be wrong -- AZ1005 explicitly marks both) but **when flowering meets the pollen-viability threshold**. Frost does not bind either: an Aug 1 sowing at 80-110 DTM harvests Oct 20 - Nov 19 against a first frost of Dec 15 (z9) / Dec 31 (z10-11).

**OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN: the desert July planting note.** There is **no rendering home for it.** plant-astro reads **none** of `region_notes_seasoned`/`region_notes_beginner`, `planting_note`, `zone_notes` or `notes` -- and `zone_notes`/`notes` were *deliberately* dropped (`PlantingCalendarCard.astro:375`). The one dual-register field that **does** render for a second planting is `succession_policy.tip_seasoned`/`tip_beginner`, and it is **crop-level**, so desert heat copy written there would leak onto `fl_peninsula` and `rgv`, which carry the same second planting and are humid subtropical. Writing prose now would produce something no user ever sees. Ship the frontend first (`fail-open-renderer-hides-new-values`).

## 2026-08-03 (campaign A) -- 52 California bare-UC citations repointed at the table that backs them (`38a579d4` -> `e65aa63a`)

Kickoff 50, campaign A of four. **Citation-only: not one value moved, not one source id changed, no finding filed.** 178 `anchoring_urls` entries / 89 nodes / **52 (crop, region, source) decisions** / 8 crops (acorn-squash, butternut-squash, spaghetti-squash, pumpkin, cantaloupe, honeydew-melon, watermelon, okra). Arc count **167 -> 115** decisions, SOLE pairs **614 -> 436**, SOLE nodes **414 -> 325** -- all three deltas match the footprint exactly.

**BOTH OF THE KICKOFF'S GATING TASKS FIRED, AND BOTH CHANGED THE CAMPAIGN.**

**1. The count reconciliation is settled: the shipped scan is RIGHT and has no bug.** Kickoff 50 §2 flagged `citation_provenance_scan.py` (167 decisions / 32 hunts, California 76 over 8) against a hand traversal giving 77 over 7 with `ca_desert`/`uc_mg` at 2 and `ca_south_coast`/`ucanr_ext` at 21. An independent re-derivation written this session -- walking canonical from scratch, **not** importing the scan -- reproduces the tool exactly: 614 pairs, 414 nodes, 167 decisions, 32 hunts, California 76 with the identical per-hunt split. `region_of()`'s regex was then checked against a **structurally**-determined region (which key of `regions{}` the node descends from) on every node carrying `anchoring_urls`: **0 disagreements**. The hand traversal applied `len(sources) == 1` to the **REGION ROOT**, whose value child nodes inherit -- `plantings[]` nodes carry `anchoring_urls` but **no `sources` key of their own**. That rule reproduces all three of its distinctive signatures (7 hunts, `ca_desert`/`uc_mg` = 2, `ca_interior`/`uc_mg` absent entirely -- the missing 8th hunt). **The generalizable lesson: a node naming TWO bare hosts is not "sourced."** SOLE must mean *every source cited here is a domain root*, never *the list has one entry*.

**2. Re-verification killed two of the kickoff's four authoring decisions -- and the stale record was a kickoff's own "do NOT redo this" section.** Fourth occurrence of `stale-records-commission-phantom-work`, and the worst shape yet, because a section headed *do not redo this* is the last place anyone re-verifies. Pumpkin's `Jan 15 - Feb 15`, billed as **"the one real DATA-defect candidate"**, no longer exists: corrected twice (to `Feb 1 - Mar 1`, then re-derived to **`Mar 1 - Mar 15`**) with `pumpkin_desert_spring_march_rederivation` marked **`resolved`**. And §3 row 1 recommended repointing the winter-squash fall cycle at **AZ1005 -- the exact move the accepted finding `ca_desert_fall_cycle_provenance_gap` had already REFUSED BY NAME** as *"the geography stretch the arc warns about"*. **A record can be stale in the RECOMMENDATION, not just the value:** checking that a quoted number still exists is not enough; check whether a later ruling already adjudicated the move the record proposes.

**CAMPAIGN A IS THREE CLASSES, NOT ONE.** The split was invisible while it was priced as "one document, four regions, two source ids": **52 clean repoints + 12 blocked by a contradicted cell** (8 on the ruled fall-cycle gap, 4 on the two live okra calls) **+ 12 with NO UC ROW AT ALL**. That last class is the substantive find -- the target page is **Table 13.2, a VEGETABLE table** (artichoke -> watermelons), standing as sole source on `lemon` 4, `lime` 3, `arugula` 2, `pear-asian`/`pear-european`/`edamame` 1 each. That is the `vce_426_331` shape living inside campaign A. **`lemon` + `lime` are 7 of the 12 and overlap campaign D's lemon cluster** -- work them together, not twice.

**THE DOCUMENT.** Re-fetched from raw bytes this session (`urllib`, 71,434 bytes) and parsed by **HTML structure with a rectangularity assertion** (33x6), never a WebFetch markdown parse, which silently shifts columns on an HTML data table -- and this block is entirely a table-reading exercise. The region definitions and the *"planting dates are only approximate"* caveat came back **byte-identical** to the 2026-07-29 transcription, so the document has not moved. Re-adjudicated 92 windows: **48 SUPPORTED / 28 DIVERGENT / 16 CONTRADICTED**, and 12 of the 16 contradicted cells are already ruled. **DIVERGENT rides along** -- absorbed by the source's own caveat, not a defect class.

**WHY A URL REPOINT AND NOT A NEW SOURCE ID.** Both ids **already** cite this exact pathed URL elsewhere -- `ucanr_ext` on 578 nodes, `uc_mg` on 126. The bare hosts are the outliers, so the fix makes these nodes agree with the 704 that already name the document. No `source_catalog` entry added, no `sources` array touched, no id collapsed -- deliberately smaller than `promote_mid_south_fruit_tree_repoint.py`'s new-id pattern, which was needed there only because `uada_ext` carried two different URLs.

**THE MIXED-CLAIM NODE, stated rather than glossed.** The 89 nodes are 63 `resolved_by_zone.<z>` cells and 26 `plantings[<i>]` arms, each carrying a planting window **and** harvest fields under one `anchoring_urls` block, while Table 13.2 publishes planting dates only. The harvest half is not thereby misattributed: **all 8 crops carry an ACCEPTED `*_pilot_regional_calendars_modeled` finding** declaring those windows MODELED from days-to-maturity plus the frost anchors. So the planting half becomes citable and the harvest half stays declared-as-derived. No dedicated harvest, bloom, start-indoors or heat-pause arm is in the repoint set.

**TREVOR RULED (2026-08-03):** leave all 8 cucurbit decisions blocked by the fall-cycle gap. Their *main* windows are supported and only the second planting is not, so node-granular repointing would recover them -- but it would split one region's anchors across two URLs, which is what `mid_south`'s one-id-one-URL rule exists to prevent. Revisit only if the fall-cycle gap is ever closed by edit.

**MUTATION TESTING FOUND 8 OF 21 GUARDS VACUOUS on the first pass -- the FIFTH occurrence in this repo.** Six needed a shim to become reachable at all: the two constant-vs-constant checks (a held pair leaking into the worklist; an unparseable transcribed row), a **typo'd `NEW_URL` that is still a bare host** (a realistic failure the post-condition existed for and could never see), a doctored `before`-snapshot for the held-pair-modified and crops-changed guards, and a **node-count drift that holds the entry count constant** (move one anchor to a new node: entries stay 178, nodes become 90). Two checks that could not fail under **any** input -- the decision-count abort and a "slipped through" fallback -- were **REMOVED rather than left standing as decoration**, since a check that cannot fail is not a guard. Re-run after the fixes: **19/19 real, 0 vacuous**.

## 2026-07-31 (herb hardiness attributions) -- ten University of Arkansas credits that were NC State's (`c6f50a14` -> `38a579d4`)

Kickoff 49, worked end to end. **10 attributed sentences / 7 cells / 5 crops** (thyme, rosemary, oregano, sage, lavender). Attribution only: no number, suitability, citation, arm or calendar moved.

**THE WORKLIST WAS RE-MEASURED, NOT TAKEN FROM THE KICKOFF.** It matched exactly (thyme 1, rosemary 2, oregano 1, sage 2, lavender 4), which is worth recording precisely because the previous three kickoffs did not survive that test.

**WHAT THE PROSE IS.** `mid_south` is the `mid_atlantic` prose with the region words swapped and the institution find-and-replaced. The citations settle it: every `mid_atlantic` herb cell anchors to the real NC State Plant Toolbox page **for the exact species** (`thymus-vulgaris`, `salvia-rosmarinus`, `origanum-vulgare`, `salvia-officinalis`, `lavandula-angustifolia`), while every `mid_south` herb cell anchors to `https://www.uaex.uada.edu`, a bare host. Read from raw bytes, NC State's `USDA Plant Hardiness Zone` field matches our numbers **to the character** on four of five -- thyme `5a-9b`, sage `4a-8b`, lavender `5a-9b`, oregano floor `4a` -- and lavender's disease sentence is verbatim Toolbox ("susceptible to leaf spot and root rot. Root rot is caused by overwatering").

**ADJUDICATED PER CROP, AND THE ANSWERS GENUINELY DIFFER** -- the apple/pawpaw trap the kickoff warned about. UAEX publishes **no** hardiness zone for four of the five species. Its entire herb reference desk is a Janet Carson Q&A column that contains no `zone` token at all, and its sidebar **enumerates** the desk (Basil, Chives, Oregano, Parsley, Rosemary, Thyme, Wild Garlic/Onion) -- **no sage, no lavender**, which is stronger evidence than the two 404s. Parsing all **1,197** Plant of the Week archive links returns nine entries touching these taxa, and their Latin names disqualify almost all of them: creeping thyme is *Thymus praecox* (our crop is *T. vulgaris*), the only *Origanum* is the ornamental hybrid 'Amethyst Falls', and the four "sages" are *Salvia greggii*, *Perovskia atriplicifolia*, *Salvia elegans* (zones 8-10) and *Salvia nemorosa* (zones 4-9) -- **none is *Salvia officinalis***. **The trap of the whole hunt: the one archive page that pairs a zone range with the word "rosemary" is "Willow Rosemary" -- *Salix elaeagnos*, a WILLOW.** A name-matching scan would have accepted it.

**LAVENDER IS THE EXCEPTION AND THE BIGGER FIND (kickoff §4.5).** UAEX **does** publish a hardiness range for our exact species: its English Lavender Plant of the Week (Gerald Klingaman, 2007-07-20) states *"Lavender is hardy from **zones 5 to 8**."* We credited UAEX with **"zones 5a to 9b"** -- NC State's number. The same page **does** support the humidity framing ("Wet soils, especially during wintertime, cause root rot", "High summer humidity is not to its liking") but **never mentions leaf spot**, and "plant profile" is Toolbox vocabulary. Surfaced rather than quietly aligned.

**THE FIX IS PURELY SUBTRACTIVE** -- the `cherry-sweet` precedent, and the target shape already sat in these same cells (`thyme` z7 `grown_as_note_seasoned` reads "Thyme is hardy to about zone 4 to 5" with no institution). Every retained number is corroborated by the crop's own record, so nothing is stranded: `hardiness_zone_min/max` of 4/9, 7/10, 4/9, 4/8, 5/9, and the pilot findings that set them. **`rosemary_pilot_finding_004` is the one that matters most** -- it records 7 as our own *hardy-cultivar-inclusive* floor ("Hill Hardy z7, Arp z6") while explicitly noting the species is z8 per NCSU, which is why the number survives the credit's removal. **The credit was NOT repointed to NC State:** these arms do not carry `ncsu_ext`, and naming a source the arm does not carry is exactly what the hunt-1 guard refuses.

**TWO FINDINGS FILED, EACH ITS OWN RULING.** `lavender_mid_south_uaex_zone_range_divergence`: if `mid_south` lavender is ever repointed to UAEX's real Plant of the Week URL -- the one genuine repoint this hunt found, and the fix for its bare host -- the z8 cell **must** change with it, since it reads "zone 8 sits comfortably inside ... zone 5 to 9b" and under UAEX's number zone 8 is the **ceiling**. `rosemary_mid_atlantic_ncsu_zone_attribution`: `mid_atlantic` credits NC State with "zone 7 to 8" but the Toolbox says `8a-10b`; the number is sound, the credit overstates, and it is a different region so out of this hunt's scope.

**MUTATION TESTING CAUGHT THREE VACUOUS GUARDS OF MY OWN** -- the fourth occurrence in three days. The first pass protected 13 of 16 checks; deleting the top-level-key, other-regions and trailing-newline guards left the suite **green**, because no test could reach them. Fixed by adding a `before`-snapshot doctoring shim (simulating a change the EDITS loop never made) and a `json.dumps` shim, after which **16/16** guards fail a test when deleted. The suite also pins **abort messages, not just exit codes**, deliberately: the post-edit "zero attributions remain" sweep is a strict superset of the preflight count, so exit-code-only assertions would have stayed green with the preflight deleted.

**ALSO A LESSON IN READING THE FAILURE.** `whole_crop_gate` appeared to fail on all five crops; the output was a `FileNotFoundError` from my own wrong invocation (it takes a positional slug, not `--slug`), and `gate_all` was passing 121/121 the whole time. Read the output before believing the exit code.

**GAUNTLET:** guards **26/26 on BOTH runners**; full suite **338 -> 364 passed**; `gate_all` 121/121 and **byte-identical to the pre-state capture**; `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all 5 touched crops; all 5 standalone gates exit 0 **and byte-identical to the pre-state capture**; `release_verify` against the saved pre-state differs from an unchanged-baseline run by **exactly two lines** (the crops-changed CONCERN naming exactly the 5, and "lavender regions changed: ['mid_south']") -- the pre-existing `rgv` novel-key CONCERN is unmoved; COMPACT preserved, no trailing newline. `c6f50a14` registered in `promote_fixture.COMMIT_FOR` -> `761a128`. **NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED.**

## 2026-07-31 (cleanup batch) -- the two schema-shape defects the audit's framing had wrong (`172e4e7a` -> `e353fadb` -> `c6f50a14`)

Trevor-ruled as "the unblocked and cheap ones". Two guarded promotes, both footprint-exact.

**PROMOTE 1 (`e353fadb`) -- artichoke's `open_findings` sat where nothing reads them.** 12 findings relocated under `verification_status`, byte-for-byte. Artichoke was the **only crop of 128** storing them at the top level; 120 use the nested key and 7 uncertified shells have neither. Every gate and scan reads the nested key -- `whole_crop_gate` line 1062 is `vs.get("open_findings") or []` -- so artichoke was silently skipped and **every roster finding count in this repo was short by 12**. The external blind audit's 768 is really **780**, and its "62 crops with unfinished findings" excluded artichoke entirely. **Origin found in source rather than guessed:** `tools/promote_artichoke.py` line 340 writes `crop["open_findings"] = copy.deepcopy(prose.OPEN_FINDINGS)` -- the cert promote used the wrong path. A bug, not an archetype choice; asparagus, the other herbaceous perennial, uses the nested key. **Explicitly not an emergency, and the guard prints it:** all 12 are `status: accepted` with `blocks_launch: false`, so nothing that would have blocked certification was hidden. The cost was measurement integrity, not a shipped defect. **Scope held to relocation:** the entries also use `title` + `note_internal` where the roster uses `summary`, but `summary` is read by NO gate and NO general scan (only one-off promote scripts pinned to a named finding, one of which already falls back to another key), so normalizing that is a separate ruling and was left alone. Guards 15/15 both runners.

**PROMOTE 2 (`c6f50a14`) -- asparagus's five missing top-level fields, backfilled as `null`.** **THE RECORD WAS WRONG AND THIS IS THE POINT OF THE ENTRY.** Kickoff 48 §4 records asparagus's 7 missing fields as *"a perennial-schema question, not an omission to backfill"*. Measured: 56 top-level keys appear on >=90% of the 128 crops, asparagus lacks exactly 7 and is the **sole** crop missing each, and **artichoke -- the only other `herbaceous_perennial` -- lacks none of the 56.** The archetype is not the explanation. Each `null` rests on a convention re-measured against the file rather than quoted: **36 of the 37** crops with `days_to_maturity == []` carry `days_to_maturity_mid: null` and **zero** carry a value, so asparagus is the 37th; `propagule == "crown"` means no indoor start exists for `weeks_indoors`, and the only other crown crop carries null; `first_planting_notify_days` (52 null), `last_reviewed` and `last_reviewed_session` (22 null each) are all null on artichoke. **`null` is the honest value, not a shape being filled** -- writing a date into `last_reviewed` would assert a top-level review that never happened, which is the lettuce-leaf `verified` defect one field over. Guards 12/12 both runners, including premise checks that ABORT if DTM is ever populated or the propagule stops being `crown` (a null is only correct while those hold), plus a sabotage proving a non-null backfill is refused.

**TWO OF THE SEVEN DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, each its own ruling:** `yield_expectations` is present **and non-null on all 127 other crops** (zero nulls roster-wide), so a null would assert "no yield data exists" when the truth is "nobody authored it" -- it needs real dual-register authoring with T1 sources, like artichoke's USU/TAMU-sourced block. `zones` is the one genuine schema question, and plant-astro's `today.ts`, `[crop]/[zone].astro` and `TreeGuide.astro` read `zones{}` and **fail open**, so the consumer behaviour must be checked before choosing placeholder-vs-absent.

**WHY NOTHING CAUGHT EITHER:** `whole_crop_gate` PASSES on both asparagus and artichoke and references none of the seven fields. `optional-field-gates-go-vacuous`, third occurrence.

**MUTATION-TESTING AGAIN CAUGHT A VACUOUS GUARD OF MY OWN.** `test_aborts_if_the_nested_key_already_exists` passed with the refusal deleted, because injecting the nested key also pushes the nested-crop count 120 -> 121 and the count preflight aborts first. Rewritten to drop another crop's nested key so the count stays 120 and the refusal is the only check standing. Same lesson as the de-zone pass hours earlier: a guard that has never been shown failing is not yet a guard.

**GAUNTLET (both promotes):** guards 27/27 across the two suites on BOTH runners; `gate_all` 121/121 after each; `whole_crop_gate` PASS on artichoke and asparagus; all 5 standalone gates exit 0 **and byte-identical to the pre-state capture** after each; `release_verify` against the rebuilt pre-state differs by **exactly one line** each time (the expected crops-changed CONCERN naming only `artichoke`, then only `asparagus`); COMPACT preserved with byte-identical re-serialization; suite **311 -> 338 passed**. `e353fadb` registered in `promote_fixture.CHAIN` (replay from `172e4e7a`), `172e4e7a` in `COMMIT_FOR` -> `7092ca1`. NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED.

**ALSO MEASURED, NOT FIXED:** `pet_safe` is recorded COMPLETE in memory but `tools/pet_safe_coverage.py` reports **logged=114 of 121 certified** with 7 VIOLATIONs -- artichoke, asparagus, dry-bean, field-corn, flint-corn, popcorn, sweet-corn. The rollout log is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-06-pet-safe-rollout-log.json`, dated **before all 7 were certified**, so this is a stale completeness record rather than a regression. ## 2026-07-31 -- 66 zone-span-lifted rows told the reader they were in the DONOR zone (`8d2b1a91` -> `172e4e7a`)

**Trevor-ruled:** *"I don't want anything reader visible being incorrect."* 106 prose strings / 66 cells / 15 crops. Prose only; no value, date, calendar, citation or lift marker moved.

**How it was found.** Not by a gate and not by looking for it. While adjudicating the `ucr_citrus` hunt (below) I read `grapefruit ca_south_coast z11` and its own copy said *"Zone 10 on the south coast almost never freezes"*. Reading the cell is what surfaced it, which is the arc's whole method.

**Mechanism, confirmed in source rather than inferred.** `tools/build_zonespan_widen_patch.py` reconciles five warm regions to the 2023 USDA map with `row = copy.deepcopy(rbz[donor]); row["lifted_from_zone"] = donor` -- and no prose rewrite. **The DATA call was right**: the map moved the cities the regions were authored for (Phoenix 9b->10a, Honolulu ->z12, warm CA coast ->z11), so the row genuinely is that city's data, and `lifted_from_zone` records the lift honestly. What shipped wrong is the SENTENCE. A correct data operation introduced a rendering-honesty defect, which is why no gate saw it -- `region_prose_gate --all` returns 0, and its ZONE-SPAN check does not cover this class.

**The blast radius is exactly the widen's own footprint:** 65 of the 66 sit on a `lifted_from_zone` row (1,855 exist; 1,789 are clean because their prose never names a zone), and the affected (region, zone) pairs are precisely the zones carried by **113** crops rather than 120 -- `ca_south_coast` z11, `ca_desert` z11, `hawaii_tropical` z10/z12/z13, `low_desert_az` z10, `se_gulf` z10.

**DE-ZONED, NOT RENUMBERED, and that is a correctness call, not a style one.**
- Renumbering asserts zone-specific claims we cannot source. The decisive case: mandarin's `ca_south_coast` cell names the **Ojai Pixie**, and Ojai is not zone 11. Renumbering would have relocated a named place into the wrong zone -- manufacturing a new defect while fixing an old one.
- De-zoning is safe for every NUMBER in the copy **because it was checked first**: each donor->lifted pair carries an identical `region_chill_delivered` band (`low_desert_az` 9/10 `[100,400]`; `ca_south_coast` 10/11 `[50,350]`; `ca_desert` 10/11 `[100,300]`; `hawaii_tropical` 10-13 `[0,150]`; `se_gulf` 9/10 `[350,650]`). Had they differed, renumbering and de-zoning would BOTH have been wrong and the fix would have needed re-authoring per zone. 8 witness figures (`about 100 to 300 hours`, `roughly 50 to 350 hours`, `below 27°F`, ...) are re-asserted by the guard.
- Each rule swaps only the zone-naming noun phrase; the tail stays byte-identical, which is what keeps this a label correction rather than a rewrite. Region wording was chosen to preserve the warm-end sense: `se_gulf`'s becomes *"The Gulf coast"*, not *"The Gulf"*, because the region also holds z8 where *"mostly safe for mandarins"* would be false.

**A COUNT IS A QUESTION, AGAIN.** The naive regex reports **430**; the honest number is **106**. Most hits are legitimate comparative prose (*"hardy to about zone 5"*, *"nearer than zone 8's"*). Per the standing lesson the CHECK was narrowed, not the scope. The one surviving false positive -- pawpaw `ca_interior` z9, *"As in interior zone 8, pawpaw is marginal here"* -- is correct copy on a non-lifted row and is deliberately untouched.

**MUTATION-TESTING CAUGHT TWO VACUOUS GUARDS OF MY OWN, which is the reusable lesson.** Both were green and both were worthless:
1. `test_comparative_prose_is_not_flagged` passed with the comparative guard **deleted** -- pawpaw's row is not lifted, so the lifted-row filter excluded it before the guard ever ran. Fixed by putting a comparison on a LIFTED row, where the filter cannot save it.
2. `test_..._extra_prose_edit` passed with the footprint **count check deleted** -- the sabotage added a NEW key, tripping the structural check first. Fixed by mutating an EXISTING clean prose key on a lifted row, the one case only the count can catch.
A third correction was mine too: the first collateral-damage test sabotaged the *fixture* and expected an abort, which never came, correctly -- the guard checks what the promote CHANGES, and a value already present is not collateral damage. Rewritten to sabotage `apply()` in-process.

**And this suite broke its own promote.** `test_dezone_lifted_prose` initially read LIVE canonical, so the moment the pass landed, 2 tests failed reporting 0 defects. Repointed at the pre-state rebuilt by `promote_fixture.pre_state(BASE_SHA)` -- the exact fix the 2026-07-30 vacuity work prescribed -- plus a new `TestShippedState` asserting live canonical stays clean. `8d2b1a91` registered in `promote_fixture.COMMIT_FOR` -> `073d358`.

**GAUNTLET.** Guards **37/37 on BOTH runners**; `whole_crop_gate` PASS on all 15 touched crops; `gate_all` **121/121**; all five standalone gates exit 0 **and byte-identical to the pre-state capture**; `release_verify` against the rebuilt pre-state differs by **exactly one line**, the expected crops-changed CONCERN naming the 15 intended crops (the known single-crop-pilot shape), with *"no new violations introduced"* and *"no `--`/em-dash/spelled-degrees in any user-facing string"*; `region_prose_gate --all` 0; `internal_contradiction_scan` totals **unmoved** (CHILL 34 / TYPE 11 / DATES 35 / TEMPLATE 24 / SUIT 74), as a prose-only pass should leave them; COMPACT preserved with byte-identical re-serialization; suite **274 -> 311 passed**. NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED.

## 2026-07-31 (investigation) -- `ucr_citrus`, the arc's "cheapest closure", rests on a FALSE PREMISE

**Canonical untouched by this half.** Kickoffs 46, 47 and 48 all carry the same shovel-ready item: *"`ucr_citrus`: 33 pairs / 4 crops, ONE METHOD -- the UCR accession pages carry 'Season of ripeness at Riverside', and Riverside **is** `ca_interior`."* It traces to one row of `docs/2026-07-29-citation-cleanup-sample-pass-outcome.md`, generalized from a single observation on `crc3178` -- an **Owari Satsuma**, a mandarin -- to *"all 4 citrus crops on `ucr_citrus`'s 33 SOLE pairs"*.

**Riverside is not `ca_interior`, by our own data.** `zone_frost_data["10a"].regions.mediterranean` lists **Los Angeles LAX, San Diego, Long Beach, Riverside** -- the `ca_south_coast` set. `ca_interior` is anchored on the Central Valley: Sacramento/Fresno/Bakersfield/Modesto (8a), Tulare (8b), Stockton/Merced/Livermore (9a). Riverside appears in none of them.

**What UCR actually publishes, measured over 24 accession pages rather than inferred from one:** 24/24 carry "Season of ripeness at Riverside", so that half of the premise holds; **1/24** also carries Lindcove (which genuinely is the interior valley); and **0/24 publish a bloom date** -- all six bloom/blossom sentences are flower colour (*"white blossoms"*, *"blossoms are pure white and fragrant"*) or a qualitative pattern (*"mainly in spring"*). Third institution after UAEX and NC State with no bloom datum; per the closed-item rule this is NOT widened to the literature. **My own first probe under-reported the ripeness field as 12/24** on a whitespace-adjacency bug and was corrected by re-extraction -- the fifth artifact count in two days, and again in my own tool.

**Why the repoint would have manufactured defects.** It is a SINGLE-SITE datum with no regional resolving power: our four California grapefruit windows (Jan-May, Dec-May, Feb-Jun, Dec-May) all sit inside one location's **cultivar** spread (Marsh/Duncan Jan-May; Redblush/Rio Red/Star Ruby Feb-Jun; Oroblanco Dec-Mar), so citing it per-region converts cultivar variation at one site into regional variation. For lime it is worse than unsupportive: UCR says Oct-Dec and defines that as *"full maturity ... they drop from the tree"* (yellow, dropped fruit), while our Jul-Dec describes green-lime picking -- a different quantity, the [[harvest-start-is-not-a-published-datum]] shape.

**Settled by our own catalog, which needs no geography at all:** `source_catalog.ucr_citrus.citable_for` reads *"variety identity, characteristics, parentage, and home-grower recommendations."* It never claimed regional date windows. **31 of the 33 SOLE pairs cite it for exactly that**, so they are CASE 2 (unsourced claim), not CASE 1 (repoint). The 2 in-scope pairs are `rootstock_options[2]` (Flying Dragon) on grapefruit and orange-navel; `/crc3330A` exists and supports only the dwarfing/container claim, while the cold-hardiness ranking, Phytophthora/nematode/tristeza resistance and saline/high-pH sensitivity appear **nowhere** on UCR CVC (its rootstock overview page is a 2,981-char navigation list). Those need UC ANR's rootstock publication -- a new catalog admission -- and the 31 date pairs need a UC ANR California citrus harvest calendar, a different hunt. **Kickoffs 46/47/48 and the sample-pass doc should be corrected before anyone prices this again.**

## 2026-07-30 (tooling) -- six promote guard suites were reporting green while testing nothing

**Canonical untouched (`d77b9c51`).** Found while fixing the one Trevor asked about.

Every promote guard suite in the repo opened with:

    if not _canonical_is_base():
        print('SKIP: canonical is not the pinned base SHA')
        return

That is correct only while canonical still sits on that promote's base SHA -- and canonical moves
after **every** promote. So each suite went **silently vacuous**. Measured: **six suites running
ZERO checks**, with `cherry-sour` about to become the seventh (canonical had moved three times since
its base). **121 guard checks were not executing**, while the release gauntlet counted their green.

This is the `optional-field-gates-go-vacuous` shape applied to the guards themselves, and it is
worse than a missing test: the green is load-bearing, so nobody looks.

**THE FIX -- `tools/promote_fixture.py`.** Stop using live canonical as the fixture; rebuild the
pinned pre-state.

1. **From a commit**, where the base SHA was committed.
2. **By replay**, where it was not. Hunt 1 ran four guarded promotes back to back and committed only
   the final state, so `14c8eab2`, `5f58654b` and `d1b441c2` were working-tree states that exist in
   no commit. Each is exactly its predecessor plus one promote script, so it is rebuilt by replaying
   that script from the committed `13d42f95`. Verified byte-exact.

Every path is **hash-verified** against the requested SHA, so a wrong reconstruction cannot quietly
become a fixture, and an unresolvable SHA **raises** -- loudly, never a skip.

**THE PROOF THE FIXTURES ARE REAL.** All six suites now reproduce **exactly** the guard counts
recorded in this log when each promote was originally run: 11/11, 19/19, 28/28, 21/21, 21/21, 21/21.
A wrong pre-state could not do that. Separately, cherry-sour was adversarially checked by injecting

## 2026-07-31 (eleventh promote) -- the tomato NPK hints taught the label wrong

**Canonical `72adc366` -> `1dd6ada3` (10 edits / 5 crops, wording only). Count 128 / 121 certified unchanged.**

The external audit found three tomatoes saying *"you want the third number to be the highest"* and
then giving `5-10-10` and `8-32-16` -- in neither of which the third number is highest.

**IT IS FIVE CROPS, NOT THREE.** `beefsteak-tomato` and `heirloom-tomato` carry the same error in a
form the audit's read did not catch: *"a higher third number on the bag (like 5-10-10)"*, where the
third number is **tied** with the second, not higher.

**AND THE UNDERLYING CLAIM IS UNSOURCED, which is the bigger finding.** Both cited sources were
fetched and read in full:

- **Clemson HGIC never mentions potassium at all.** It says *"A soil test is always the best method
  of determining the fertilization needs of the crop."*
- **UMN Extension:** *"Apply phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) according to soil test
  recommendations... Unless your soil test report specifically recommends additional phosphorus, use
  a **low- or no-phosphorus** fertilizer. Too much nitrogen fertilization will lead to plants that
  are bushy, leafy, and slow to bear fruit."*

So *"make potassium the highest number"* is supported by neither, and **`8-32-16` -- phosphorus 32,
the largest number on that bag -- is the opposite of what our own cited source advises.** We were
teaching people how to read a fertilizer label and then pointing them at the one formula UMN warns
against, on the crop most likely to be a beginner's first.

**THE FIX RETREATS TO WHAT IS SOURCED** rather than inventing a replacement rule: soil test first
(both sources), go easy on nitrogen before fruit set (UMN verbatim), no added phosphorus unless a
test calls for it (UMN verbatim). `8-32-16` is removed outright; `5-10-10` stays because it IS the
crop's `npk_ratio`.

**DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED:** `npk_ratio` stays `5-10-10` on all five. Whether a phosphorus-containing
formula is the right default when UMN advises low-or-no-P is a **real open question** -- but it is a
different one, and a value change never rides along with a wording correction.

Guards **53/53 both runners**, and they assert the **content** of the replacement -- soil test
present, nitrogen warning kept, phosphorus guidance carried, `8-32-16` gone, `npk_ratio` and the
ninth promote's cadence fields frozen -- because the failure mode for a wording fix is text that
becomes self-consistent and stays wrong. `gate_all` 121/121; 5 standalone gates 0; `release_verify`
identical to pre-state.

**CONFIRMED BY OUR OWN TOOL:** `internal_contradiction_scan --family NPK` drops 11 -> 8, the three
tomatoes gone. The remaining 8 are a different shape (high-nitrogen claims on basil, cosmos, parsnip,
slicing-cucumber, sweet-alyssum, sweet-potato, tomatillo, viola) and stay open.

**NOT COMMITTED, NOT PUSHED.**

Trevor asked for these to be removed and I had recommended it. **Investigation reversed that, and
the recommendation was wrong on two independent counts.**

> `{"url": null, "verified": null, "note": "URL not in retro log, needs manual lookup"}`

That is a deliberate record of a known gap, not noise.

**2. Removing the anchor orphans the source id.** In **all 54** nodes, the null id is *also* listed
in that node's `sources`. Deleting the anchor entry leaves the source id unanchored -- which is
precisely the `src_not_anchored` mismatch class, the same shape as lettuce-leaf's 58. It would trade
57 nulls for 57 mismatches and net zero.

elsewhere in the file with a real url -- pointing at a **different document**:

|---|---|---|

| `uf_ifas_south_cal` | 9 | EDIS EP452 |
| `uc_mg` | 8 | a **bare host** (`mg.ucanr.edu`) -- gains nothing |
